title: Hide the empty thumbnail link of listing items without an image
description:
## Description In a default listing, a post with no preview image gets an empty thumbnail link. `item-default.ejs.md` wraps the thumbnail of every item in ``, and when the post has no image and the listing sets no `image-placeholder`, `emptyDiv()` in `website-listing-read.ts` fills that link with `
 
`. The link has no accessible name but is still a Tab stop, so keyboard and screen reader users meet one unnamed link per post before its title link. axe-core reports it as `link-name`. The template only knows about an image the post declares in its front matter (`image`). Otherwise it emits a placeholder comment, and `completeListingItems()` resolves it once the post has been rendered: a preview image found in the rendered page (`.preview-image`, a feature/cover/thumbnail image, or the first local image), the listing's `image-placeholder`, or the empty div. So the fix sits at that last step. When the placeholder becomes the empty div and sits directly inside a link, the link gets `aria-hidden="true"` and `tabindex="-1"`. Its other attributes are kept and the markup is otherwise unchanged, so the layout stays the same and links that do show an image are not touched. The title link next to the thumbnail goes to the same page. Before: ```html
 
``` After: ```html
 
``` I hid the link rather than removing it because that keeps the DOM identical for CSS and custom templates, and it is one of the two outcomes the issue asks for. A custom template that puts the placeholder inside a link next to other content is left alone, since that link has content of its own. The new smoke test renders a default listing with three posts (image in the front matter, image found in the rendered body, no image), once without `image-placeholder` (`index.qmd`) and once with it (`placeholder.qmd`). On `main` it fails with `Required DOM Element div.thumbnail a[aria-hidden="true"][tabindex="-1"] div.listing-item-img-placeholder is missing`; with this change it passes. Run on Windows 11 with the dev build (`configure.cmd`): ``` .\run-tests.ps1 smoke/site/render-listing-thumbnail-link.test.ts ok | 1 passed | 0 failed (3s) .\run-tests.ps1 --agent smoke/site/render-listings.test.ts smoke/site/render-listing-contents-file.test.ts smoke/site/render-listing-feed-image.test.ts smoke/site/render-blog.test.ts smoke/site/render-listing-thumbnail-link.test.ts ok | 7 passed | 0 failed (39s) ``` The `smoke-all` listing documents under `listings/image-lazy-loading/blog/`, `2026/10/12/issue-15022`, `2024/10/23/issue-10829`, `2024/12/03/issue-11580`, `2025/04/01/issue-8238` and `website/llms-txt-listing` pass as well (11 passed). `2024/10/28/issue-10311` fails on this machine with and without the change because its posts need a Python kernel that is not set up here. axe-core 4.14 on the rendered `index.html`: the `link-name` finding on `.thumbnail > .no-external[href="./posts/no-image/index.html"]` is gone, and no `aria-hidden-focus` finding appears. The `link-name` and `image-alt` findings that remain on thumbnails that do show an image come from those `` having no `alt`, which is #15038 / #7028 and not changed here. The axe-core check ran in headless Chromium (Playwright's `chromium_headless_shell`), not with a screen reader. `deno fmt --check` on `website-listing-read.ts` flags lines 18–21 (an import block); that complaint exists on `main` unchanged and I left it alone. The added code is fmt-clean and `deno lint` passes. ### Open questions 1. Hide vs remove: the issue accepts either. Hiding keeps the DOM identical; removing the `` would be a small change in the same helper if you prefer no link at all. 2. The helper hides *any* link that wraps only the placeholder, so a `table` listing with `field-links: [image]` gets the same treatment. The default table listing uses a ``, so default output is unchanged. Fine, or should it be limited to the default template? 3. The thumbnails that do show an image still have no `alt` (#15038, #7028). Left untouched on purpose; happy to follow up separately. Fixes #15066 ## Checklist I have (if applicable): - [x] referenced the GitHub issue this PR closes - [x] updated the appropriate changelog in the PR - [ ] ensured the present test suite passes (ran the listing, blog and smoke-all listing tests listed above; the full suite needs R, Python and Julia which I have not set up) - [x] added new tests - [ ] created a separate documentation PR in [Quarto's website repo](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/) and linked it to this PR (not applicable: no documented behaviour changes)

title: [Tests] Update gdtools to 0.5.2 in renv.lock
description:
The macOS jobs of the nightly built-version smoke run have failed in "Restore R packages" since 2026-10-17 ([example run](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/actions/runs/39368819446)), so no macOS test has run since then.

## Root cause

`tests/renv.lock` pins gdtools 0.5.1 from the moving P3M `cran/latest` URL. gdtools 0.5.2 reached CRAN on 2026-10-15, and P3M stopped serving the 0.5.1 macOS binary afterwards (for macOS arm64 on R 4.6, `gdtools_0.5.1.tgz` is a 404 and `gdtools_0.5.2.tgz` is served). The 2026-10-16 nightly installed a 2.0 MB binary; the 2026-10-20 nightly downloaded the 81 kB source tarball instead.

The source build fails on the runner with `ld: library 'intl' not found`, and flextable fails with it as a dependent. `renv::restore()` then stops before any test runs. This is a different failure from the cold-cache cluster in #14711, where renv reports no underlying install error.

## Fix

Update gdtools to 0.5.2 with a targeted `renv::update()`. No other package changes.

The macOS legs run only in the nightly, against the `create-release` commit, so this PR's CI does not exercise them. The first nightly after merge will.

title: Fix macOS WebKit failures in Playwright keyboard tests
description:
The Playwright macOS job of the nightly "Smoke Tests (Built Version)" has been failing on WebKit since early October. Pull request CI checks Playwright assertions on Linux only, so these tests never ran on macOS before they merged. None of the failures is a Quarto regression. They come from how WebKit on macOS handles keyboard input.

## Tab skips buttons on macOS WebKit

WebKit on macOS follows Safari's default for "Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage", which is off: Tab moves only between form fields and elements with an explicit `tabindex`, and skips buttons and links. Option+Tab visits every focusable element. Linux WebKit, Chromium and Firefox all Tab to buttons.

The tabset keyboard test (#15007) and the off-screen slide tests (#15010) press Tab to reach plain `<button>` elements, so they failed on macOS from the first nightly after each one merged. The test added with #15089 has the same pattern and would fail there too once the macOS job runs again.

These tests now press `tabKey(browserName)`, the helper from #15094 that sends Alt+Tab on WebKit. It also gives the second Tab in the off-screen slide tests a real meaning on macOS: with a plain Tab, buttons on other slides were skipped whether or not they were inert.

## ArrowDown on a focused scroll region is unreliable on macOS WebKit

The axe report overlay test "focused overlay scrolls on ArrowDown" (#14713) has failed, or passed only on retry, on every macOS run since that job started. On macOS, WebKit ignores about half of ArrowDown presses on a focused scrollable element. The keydown reaches the element and is not prevented, but nothing scrolls. A plain HTML page with a fixed, focusable overflow box and no Quarto code behaves the same way, so the overlay is not the cause. PageDown scrolled every time on both pages.

The ArrowDown variant is now skipped for WebKit on macOS only. PageDown still covers the overlay keyboard scrolling there, and Linux WebKit, Chromium and Firefox keep the ArrowDown check. The scrollable code block test from #14816 already skips its arrow-key scroll assertion on WebKit for a similar reason.

## Test plan

Pull request CI does not run Playwright on macOS, so these were checked with a one-off macOS run on my fork:

- [x] Specs before this change, WebKit on macOS: the 8 Tab tests fail
- [x] Specs after this change, WebKit on macOS: the same tests pass, 3 repeats each
- [x] ArrowDown and PageDown on the axe overlay and on a plain HTML control page, WebKit on macOS, 5 repeats each
- [x] Changed specs on Chromium and Firefox locally (Windows)
- [ ] Next macOS nightly is green on these tests

title: fix(revealjs): give the slide menu button a localisable accessible name
description:
## Description

The Reveal.js slide menu button is an `<a href="#">` with only an icon inside, so it has no accessible name and fails the axe `link-name` rule.

The `menu-ready` handler in `quarto-menu.js` now sets its `aria-label`, next to the `inert` handling from #15011, both for a normal deck and for `delay-init: true`.
The vendored `menu.js` stays untouched.
The text comes from a new language key, `revealjs-menu-button-label` ("Slide menu"), which Quarto passes to the script through the menu config.

Since an author can set that text through `language:`, the config written into the `Reveal.initialize` script now escapes `<`, so a value holding `</script>` cannot end the script early.

Playwright checks the button's name on a normal deck, after a `delay-init` build and with a language override, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
The four Reveal.js axe cases that relied on `link-name` now look for `image-alt`.
A smoke-all test covers the escaping.
No screen reader was used.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The key is only in `_language.yml`, so all 35 translations fall back to English for now.
> edit:
> - #15126

Closes #14249

title: Fix Google Scholar render failure with a CSL JSON bibliography
description:
With `google-scholar: true` and a CSL JSON bibliography (`bibliography: references.json`), rendering a document that cites anything fails with:

```
Failed to generate bibliography, rendering failed with code 64
JSON parse error: Error in $: mempty
```

Found while working on Google Scholar reference metadata in #15118. The same document renders fine without `google-scholar`, and BibTeX and CSL YAML bibliographies work with it.

The Scholar metadata converts each bibliography with `pandoc <file> -t csljson` and lets Pandoc guess the input format from the extension. For `.json`, Pandoc picks its own JSON AST reader, not CSL JSON. Pandoc citeproc reads a `.json` bibliography as CSL JSON, so the fix passes `-f csljson` for `.json` files to match. This covers both the per-page tags and the book references page, which use the same conversion.

Not a regression, this conversion has been the same since at least v1.4.

title: fix(typst): add rendering for proof, remark, and solution environments
description:
## Description

In Typst output, `proof`, `remark` and `solution` blocks went through the generic renderer as plain blocks, so `@rem-` and `@sol-` references failed with "cannot reference block".

They now use theorion frames, like theorems, with a label when the block has a crossref id.
The shared setup lives in the module `modules/theorems.lua`, with a `render_code` helper that theorems and proofs both call, so `main.lua` gains no new top-level local.

A block without a crossref id passes `number: ""` and its own prefix.
Theorion only steps the counter when `number` is `auto`, so an unnumbered remark no longer shifts the numbered remark after it, and the title reads "Proof." as before.
A block that holds only a title keeps its frame, so its label still exists for references.
A block whose id is not a crossref id still crashes in every format, as on `main`; that is #15113.

Frame titles from the language files are now written as Typst strings.
Before, a title holding `#` or `[` broke compilation, for theorems too.

The smoke-all tests check the `.typ` and the PDF text, and fail without the change.
I also looked at the simple, fancy, clouds and rainbow appearances and at a book with chapter numbering.
`pdfinfo` reports `Tagged: yes`, as on `main`; PDF/UA was not validated.

Closes #14290

title: Fix Google Scholar reference tags missing first and last page
description:
With `google-scholar: true`, the `citation_reference` tags written for bibliography entries never carry `citation_firstpage` or `citation_lastpage`. A `.bib` entry with `pages = {97--111}` gets neither, and one with `pages = {42}` gets no `citation_firstpage` either. The document's own citation does get them.

## Root cause

`googleScholarMeta` writes the page tags only from CSL `page-first` and `page-last`. Pandoc's CSL JSON for a bibliography entry only has `page` (`97--111` arrives as `97-111`). The split of `page` into first and last page is done by `pages()` in `src/quarto-core/attribution/document.ts`, which only runs for the document citation.

That split also gives wrong values for the document citation, as it only splits on a hyphen. A `page: 97–111` with an en-dash, as written in CSL JSON or YAML, becomes the first page as is. `1-3, 7-9` gives `3, 7` as last page, and `97 - 111` keeps the spaces.

## Fix

The page parsing moves to `cslPageRange` in `src/core/csl.ts`. It is used for the document citation, and for bibliography entries when `page-first` and `page-last` are not set. It splits on a hyphen, en-dash or em-dash and trims the result. For a page list like `1-3, 7-9`, only `citation_firstpage` is written, as there is no single last page to report.

title: Keep the keyboard focus where it was when a revealjs presentation is shown again
description:
## Description

Fixes #15079.

Each time the page becomes visible again, for example after switching tabs, the bundled reveal.js moved the focus to `<body>` if anything else had it (`onPageVisibilityChange()`). A reader lost their place on a link or in a chart. NVDA and JAWS, which pass the arrow keys on only while the focus is in the deck, went back to browse mode.

reveal.js does this "to ensure we can use keyboard shortcuts". But keys pressed on a link or a button reach it anyway: it ignores keys only in inputs, text areas and editable content. The keys it cannot get are the ones pressed inside a frame. So the new source patch `revealjs-0003-focus-on-return.patch` moves the focus only out of a frame, and onto the deck (with `tabindex="-1"`) rather than the body. It blurs the frame first, as reveal.js did: Playwright's Firefox, which CI runs, otherwise leaves the focus in the frame. Anywhere else, the focus stays where the reader left it.

The patch follows #15020 and #15034. `update-html-dependencies.ts` applies it after 0001 and 0002, and the bundles and maps are rebuilt from 5.1.0 with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `gulp js`, as that step does. Before adding the patch, the same build with 0001 and 0002 alone reproduced all four committed files byte for byte. That needed the sources the committed maps embed with CRLF line endings to have CRLF line endings in the build too. With 0003, only `js/reveal.js`'s source and the mappings change in the maps.

Every reveal.js release from 3.9.2 to 6.0.2 does this, so I'm reporting it to reveal.js as well.

## Validation

- `revealjs-visibility-focus.spec.ts`, with a new fixture, checks what happens after the page is hidden and shown again:
  - a focused link keeps the focus;
  - a focused frame hands it to the deck;
  - the deck keeps it;
  - a focus on the body stays there;
  - after the first two, <kbd>→</kbd> still changes slides.

  Playwright does not hide the page when another tab comes to the front, so the test marks the page hidden and then visible and dispatches `visibilitychange`. The first three fail without the patch.
- All revealjs Playwright specs pass in Chromium, except `revealjs-multiplex.spec.ts`, which needs the multiplex server that the CI wrapper starts. `revealjs-visibility-focus.spec.ts` also passes in Firefox 158 over WebDriver BiDi. WebKit and Playwright's own Firefox were not run locally.
- The three patches apply in order to a pristine 5.1.0 tree with `git apply --ignore-space-change`.

title: Add install note when an extension's owner folder is not kept
description:
Follow-up to #14010, from #15111. When an extension is stored under an owner folder in its source, such as `_extensions/quarto-journals/acm/` in a local copy of the acm template, `quarto add` and `quarto use template` install it without that folder. A document using the qualified format name `quarto-journals/acm-pdf` then fails with `Unable to read the extension 'quarto-journals/acm'`, and nothing at install time says why.

## Root cause

This is the install design since 2022. The namespace of an installed extension comes from where it is installed from: the GitHub owner, or none for a local path or an archive ([docs](https://quarto.org/docs/extensions/distributing.html#archive-distribution)). An owner folder found in the source is not kept, so a fork or copy installed from another owner can't overwrite the original extension. Keeping the source owner folder was considered and dropped for this reason.

The documented source layout is `_extensions/<name>/`. The `quarto-journals/acm` repo stores its extension under an owner folder by accident, as noted in #14008.

## Fix

`readAndCopyExtensions()` in `src/extension/install.ts`, used by `quarto add`, `quarto update` and `quarto use template`, now prints which id the extension was installed as when its source owner folder differs from the install owner:

```
'quarto-journals/acm' installed as 'acm', as extensions from a local path or an archive have no owner. Refer to it as 'acm'.
'quarto-journals/agu' installed as 'quarto-ext/agu', under the owner it is installed from. Refer to it as 'agu' or 'quarto-ext/agu'.
```

Tests cover a local directory, a cross-owner GitHub template (`quarto-ext/manuscript-template-vscode` ships `quarto-journals/agu`), and no note when the owners match.

This also adds `llm-docs/extension-install-architecture.md`, describing the namespace rule and its history, the install pipeline, the extension lookup and what the tests cover, with a pointer in `.claude/rules/extensions/install.md`.

The installed layout and the expected source layout will be documented on quarto.org in a separate quarto-web PR.

Related to #15111

title: Support Pandoc floating tables and native two-column table layouts
description:
## Description

Related to #14846.

Markdown tables in `classoption: twocolumn` documents currently produce
`longtable`, which fails during PDF compilation. Upgrade the bundled Pandoc to
3.10.1 and automatically use its `.float` class for ordinary native tables,
including cross-referenced tables. Single-column documents retain the existing
default and can opt into `.float` individually. For floating cross-referenced
tables, `tbl-pos` supplies the placement unless `latex-placement` is explicitly set.

Extend native table layouts to full-width and margin tables, bottom captions,
and unlabelled panel tables. Pandoc serializes the complete table body, preserving
widths, merged cells, citations, and table notes; Quarto supplies the enclosing
environment and captions where needed.

When loading `sidenotes`, preserve both the document class's native `table*` and
`figure*` definitions and the package's margin-wide versions. Select between them
at use time so double-column floats retain their full text width, including
documents that switch columns in the body.

Automatic selection uses explicit `classoption: twocolumn`; it does not infer
unknown journal-class defaults or parse arbitrary column-switching commands.
Such documents can explicitly use `.float` or a full-width layout class.
Existing raw `longtable` conversion paths remain outside this change.

### Validation

- Deno type checking and all nine tests in
  `tests/smoke/crossref/tables-float.test.ts` and
  `tests/smoke/crossref/latex.test.ts` pass.
- Actual LuaLaTeX compilation checks numbering, subtable references, margin
  captions, column switching, citations, and notes. Runtime dimension assertions
  check that double-column floats retain the full text width.
- LaTeX assertions cover scalar/list class options, explicit `.float`, placement
  precedence, widths, merged cells, and avoidance of nested table floats.
- `deno fmt --check` for the changed TypeScript and `git diff --check` pass.
- The complete repository test suite has not been run locally.

Additional local validation used four arXiv documents with the project's Markdown
table serializer disabled. An adapter mapped its layout settings to native Quarto
attributes; the independent HTML-table converter remained enabled. All four
compiled, retained their page counts (23 / 7 / 50 / 25), and preserved all 36
table-label numbers. Extracted PDF text matched the baseline after removing
whitespace, with no unresolved references or increase in overflow warnings.
Ara supplies five native Markdown tables; the other papers primarily exercise raw
LaTeX passthrough. These local benchmark artifacts are not included in this PR;
the synthetic regression fixtures are included.

title: Keep the keyboard focus in the deck when its revealjs slide is left
description:
## Description

Fixes #15078.

Since #15010, a slide that is left becomes `inert`. When it held the keyboard focus, for example on a link the reader tabbed to, the browser dropped the focus to `<body>`. NVDA and JAWS pass the arrow keys on to reveal.js only while the focus is in the deck, so after one slide change they went back to browse mode until Tab was pressed again.

`updateInertSlides()` in the support plugin now moves the focus to the deck, made focusable with `tabindex="-1"`, before it makes the slide that has the focus inert. This also covers leaving the overview with the focus on another slide. A focus outside the slide being left is not touched. A `slidechanged` handler that focuses something on the new slide still can, since this one runs first, in the capture phase.

No changelog entry: the focus drop came with #15010, which is not released yet, so #14795's entry covers it.

## Validation

- Three Playwright tests in `revealjs.spec.ts`, next to #14795's:
  - moving on from the slide that has the focus hands it to the deck, and Tab then goes into the new slide;
  - a focus that is not on that slide is left alone;
  - leaving the overview hands a focus on another slide to the deck.

  The first and third fail without the change.
- All revealjs Playwright specs pass in Chromium, except `revealjs-multiplex.spec.ts`, which needs the multiplex server that the CI wrapper starts. Firefox and WebKit were not run locally.

title: Fix duplicate Scholar citation_reference for a key in two bibliography files
description:
With `google-scholar: true` and a key defined in two bibliography files, the page gets two `citation_reference` tags for it. Pandoc renders a single entry, the one from the later file, so the extra tag can describe a work that is not shown on the page. No GitHub issue exists; found while reviewing #15106.

## Root cause

`renderToCSLJSON` concatenates the CSL entries of each bibliography file in order without deduplicating ids, and `citationReferenceMeta` writes one tag per matching entry. The per-page postprocessor and the book references page both consume this list, so both are affected. Listing the same file twice is not affected, since the `bibliography` metadata merge already deduplicates it. The concatenation predates the recent Scholar changes.

## Fix

`renderToCSLJSON` now resolves a repeated id the way Pandoc does, with the later file's entry replacing the earlier one. The kept entry stays at the position where the id first appeared, ids are compared exactly (`Case` and `case` stay two entries), and entries without an id pass through. Fixing it in this shared helper means `format-html-meta.ts` is unchanged.

Later-file-wins is observed Pandoc behavior: the manual only documents inline `references` taking precedence over bibliography files. The smoke test therefore also checks that the visible entry is the one the tag describes.

Inline `references` metadata is still ignored by Scholar; that is a separate problem and not changed here.

title: Fix website categories containing backticks or backslashes
description:
When a website page has a category whose backtick runs get longer after the first one, like ``a`b``c``, the category in the page title block shows broken text: ```html
Str "a`bc”``{=pandoc-native}
``` A category containing a backslash either fails the whole render with `couldn't read native` (a Windows path like `C:\x\y`), or is silently changed (`a\nb` becomes a line break, `c\\d` becomes `c\d`). ## Root cause Both come from `pandocNativeStr` in `src/core/pandoc/codegen.ts`, which writes the text as a `Str "..."` raw inline in `pandoc-native` format: 1. The inline code delimiter was sized from the first backtick run of the text, not the longest, so a later and longer run closed it early. The variable was already named `maxBackticks`. The same slip in `pandocBlock` is fixed in #14767. 2. Only `"` and newlines were escaped for the Haskell string literal the native reader parses, so a backslash started an escape sequence. The same function also writes the reveal.js URL and plugin script paths. ## Fix The delimiter is now one backtick longer than the longest run, and backslashes are escaped before the other escapes. title: fix(website/listing): resolve category links to nearest parent listing
description:
## Description

When a post appears in more than one listing, its category links could point at the wrong one.
In #14493, a post under `blog/` that the home page also lists linked its categories to `index.html#category=...`, which does not filter anything.

`findNearestParentListing` never matched, because it compared a path without a leading slash against listing paths that have one.
So the choice fell to the referrer, or to the first entry in `listings.json`, whose order depends on how the site was rendered.
It now keeps the deepest listing whose directory holds the post.

The listing the reader came from still wins when the nearest one is no more specific: the site root listing, or another listing in the same directory.
The referrer is compared by pathname and origin, so this also works on a site served under a subpath.

The Playwright tests serve `listings.json` in two explicit orders, with the home page listing last and first, as the rendered order differs between machines.
Each one fails without its fix in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
An axe scan of the test site finds the same issues with and without this change.

Fixes #14493

title: fix(mermaid): emit mermaid diagrams in a raw html block
description:
## Description

A `mermaid` diagram with its own `---` configuration block hid the rest of the document, and `ojs` cells after it never ran.
The diagram source went into the intermediate markdown as a bare `<pre>`, so its closing `---` was read as the start of YAML front matter.

The `<pre>` now goes inside a `{=html}` raw block, which the markdown splitter does not look into.
The HTML output is the same, because Pandoc already read the bare `<pre>` as an HTML raw block.

`pandocBlock` now sizes that fence from the longest backtick run in the content, not the first one.
Before, a diagram with a single backtick in one label and a line starting with three backticks later on closed the raw block early.

The commented-out tooltip code is gone, since Mermaid 11.12 creates `.mermaidTooltip` itself.

The smoke-all test covers both cases, and the backtick case fails when the fence change is reverted.
A Playwright test checks that the SVG keeps `aria-roledescription`, `<title>` from `accTitle` and `<desc>` from `accDescr` in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
It guards Mermaid's own accessibility output, which the raw block must keep.

Closes #14765

title: Quote brand font family names in the generated CSS
description:
## Description

Fixes #14882.

`brandTypographyLayer` now runs family values through `asCssFont`, the same helper the `mainfont`/`monofont` path uses, so `Source Sans 3` comes out as `"Source Sans 3"`. That's enough for `html`.

`revealjs` needed one more step. reveal.js' `exposer.scss` builds `--r-main-font`, `--r-heading-font` and `--r-code-font` with `#{$mainFont}` etc., and interpolation drops the quotes again. That also means `mainfont: Source Sans 3` is broken in `revealjs` today, not only the brand path. Rather than edit the vendored file, `quarto.scss` re-declares those three properties (plus the inline/block code font ones it already sets) with `#{inspect(...)}`, the way Bootstrap's `_root.scss` does. Quarto's rules come after the framework rules, so these win. `--mermaid-font-family` in `_quarto-rules.scss` had the same interpolation, so it got `inspect()` too.

Checked in Chromium: `body` was computing to `Times`; with this change `body`, `h2` and `code` compute to `"Source Sans 3"`, `"Bricolage Grotesque 96pt"` and `"M PLUS 1 Code"` in both `html` and `revealjs`.

Tests: `2026/10/19/issue-14882.qmd` (html) and `issue-14882-revealjs.qmd`. The revealjs one also asserts that no unquoted declaration comes after Quarto's quoted one, since `exposer.scss` still writes the unquoted value first. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. I also ran the brand tests, the revealjs tests and everything asserting on `font-family` (202 documents, 300 renders across formats): 296 pass, and the other 4 need Jupyter, LaTeX or R and fail the same way on `main` on my machine.

## Description

Fixes #14917.

Both problems from the issue came from the markdown pipeline that runs after the social meta tags are written:

- `siteTitleMetaHandler` always pushed the website title into `og:site_name`, so a page's `open-graph.site-name` never made it to the output.

title: Fix CSL markup and field separators in Scholar citation_reference tags
description:
Stacked on #15107, which adds the `cslTextToPlain` helper used here. The PR targets `fix/citation-title-markdown` and is retargeted to `main` once #15107 merges. With `google-scholar: true`, the `citation_reference` tags written for the bibliography carry CSL rich-text markup. A `.bib` title `The \emph{R} Book` gives `citation_title=The R Book`, and a journal title leaks the same way. #15107 fixes this for the document's own `citation_title`; this is the same leak in the reference tags. Two other defects show in the same tags: - fields are joined with a comma after their closing semicolon, giving `citation_title=X;,citation_author=Y;` - a chapter without a container title (an `@incollection` without `booktitle`, or a document with citation `type: chapter`) gets `citation_inbook_title=undefined`, both as a standalone tag and inside `citation_reference` ## Root cause `googleScholarReferences` passes each entry of the bibliography CSL JSON from Pandoc to `googleScholarMeta`, which writes the CSL string fields verbatim. Those fields are CSL rich text: ``, ``, ``, ``, and small caps as a `` whose `style` attribute also adds a stray semicolon inside the tag value. ## Fix Each value written into `citation_reference` goes through `cslTextToPlain`. Pandoc's `csljson` writer emits no HTML entities and only the tags the helper strips, so stripping them gives the plain text. Tag values are HTML attributes, as the [Google Scholar inclusion guidelines](https://scholar.google.com/intl/en/scholar/inclusion.html) note, so markup in them is never parsed: Scholar reads `` as literal characters in the title, not as formatting. The guidelines do not document `citation_reference`, but publishers that emit it (Springer, Copernicus, the OJS Google Scholar plugin) write plain text. Springer's `key=value` form separates fields with `; `, which the join now uses. `citation_inbook_title` is only written when `container-title` is present, as the other container branches already do. ## Checklist I have (if applicable): - [ ] referenced the GitHub issue this PR closes - [x] updated the appropriate changelog in the PR - [ ] ensured the present test suite passes - [x] added new tests - [ ] created a separate documentation PR in [Quarto's website repo](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/) and linked it to this PR

title: Fix Scholar reference tags missing on book references page
description:
#15049 limited `citation_reference` tags to the references a page actually cites or lists. In an HTML book with `google-scholar: true`, the references page itself ended up with none: a `references.qmd` holding only `::: {#refs}` got 0 tags, while the chapters were correct.

## Root cause

The per-page metadata postprocessor runs during each page's render, where the references page has an empty `#refs` div and no citations. The book post-render injects the aggregated bibliography afterwards and nothing regenerates the tags. Before #15049 every page listed all `.bib` entries, so the references page looked right by accident. #15049 is not in a release yet, so only dev builds are affected.

## Fix

After the book post-render injects the bibliography, the references page's `citation_reference` tags are regenerated from the entries now in the DOM. `format-html-meta.ts` exports `replaceGoogleScholarReferences`, built on the same id collection and tag formatting as the per-page path, so the tag content stays identical. It replaces existing tags rather than appending, so a work cited on the references page itself is not tagged twice. Reading ids from the injected `.csl-entry` elements also covers `nocite: "@*"`.

Bibliography paths are made relative to the project directory first, as `generateBibliography` does, since `renderToCSLJSON` joins them onto it.

A URL bibliography already fails the per-page path when `google-scholar` is on, so the book step uses the same loader and behaves the same way.

title: Fix raw markdown in citation title for appendix, BibTeX and Scholar
description:
When a document title contains markdown or HTML entities, the appendix citation, the BibTeX citation and the Google Scholar `citation_title` show them literally. A title `A proof system (part 1) with *emphasis*` gives `Part 1) with *Emphasis*` in the attribution, `*Emphasis*` in the BibTeX and the raw string in the Scholar meta, while the `h1` is correct. #15047 fixed the escaping of this metadata, this is the remaining part of #12452.

## Root cause

`documentCSL` takes the title as the raw YAML string, before any markdown parse:

https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/0e28ab3aedd44be2c95433a29a6aff9250fbcc75/src/quarto-core/attribution/document.ts#L104-L105

## Fix

A `quarto-pre` Lua filter takes `citation.title`, else `title`, from the main Pandoc pass, so it uses the same parse as the displayed title, and writes it with Pandoc's `csljson` writer. The result reaches the HTML postprocessors as an input trait, and `documentCSL` uses it when present. The appendix gets italics and a no-break space, the BibTeX gets `\emph{}` and `~`, and the Scholar `citation_title` gets the same title with the CSL tags stripped to plain text.

Converting in TypeScript with a separate Pandoc call was deemed too costly (one process per page and per consumer, and `documentCSL` would become async). The markdown pipeline used for website `og:` and `twitter:` metadata is only wired for websites, and would need a hand-written HTML to CSL mapping.

Math is not rendered in the citation: it keeps its TeX source (`$x^2$`), as before.

This supersedes #15048, which decoded entities before calling Pandoc. With the title already converted, that decode would turn a literal `&nbsp;` back into a no-break space. Its test cases for literal entities are kept here as a render test.

Fixes #12650

title: fix: Apply extension-contributed project metadata in quarto preview
description:
Fixes #14783.

Project metadata contributed by an extension through `contributes.metadata.project`, such as `brand`, was applied on the render path only.
The preview command builds the project context before the render services exist, so the contribution never reached the project configuration.

The merge now runs for every project context, with a fresh extension context when the render options are absent.
f6a0f8988 made that same move for engine extensions in #14208, and left the metadata merge behind the gate with the note that it needs the render options.
The merge in fact uses `services.extension` only, so this change completes that work instead of taking a different route to it.
Invalid contributed metadata stays fatal for a render, and becomes a warning that names the extension elsewhere, so a faulty extension cannot stop `quarto preview`, `quarto inspect`, `quarto publish` or `quarto serve`.
Every command that builds a project context applies the metadata now, so `quarto inspect` reports it as well.

The new tests build the context the way preview does, without render options, and cover the brand for a single file and for a project, the render path, a contributed `output-dir`, and a faulty extension.

title: feat(typst): add code annotation and filename support
description: Introduce a unified wrapper for code blocks and skylighting transformed code blocks in Typst. Add filename processing (Lua/Typst) and code-annotation processing (Lua/Typst): `filename` renders as a tab above the block, and `# ` annotations render as circled numbers at the end of each line, linked both ways with the annotation list below the block. closes #9768 ## Behaviours | Behaviour | Before (1.10) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | `filename` on a code block | Ignored, plain block. | Filename tab above the block. | | Code annotations | Stripped, replaced by a "Line N" definition list. | Circled numbers on the annotated lines, linked both ways with the annotation list. | | One annotation spanning several lines | "Lines 1-2" definition list. | A circle on each line, one shared link target. | | Annotations in a `lst-cap` cross-referenceable listing | Stripped, plain ordered list. | Circles inside the listing, annotation items after the float. | | Identifiers containing `.`/`:` (e.g. `{#lst-a.b}`) | n/a | Supported. | | `startFrom`, with or without `number-lines` | n/a | Circle follows the code line. | | Fenced-echo display blocks (```` ```{{r}} ````) | n/a | Circle lands on the code line, not the fence. | | Annotation with no trailing ordered list | n/a | Unlinked circle, render still succeeds. | | `syntax-highlighting: idiomatic` / `none` | n/a | Native path via a `raw.line` show rule. | | `syntax-highlighting: {light: ..., dark: ...}` | n/a | Resolves to the light theme, annotations keep highlighting. | | Languages unknown to Skylighting, bare blocks, code containing backtick runs, filenames needing escaping | n/a | Handled. | Any remaining mismatch (for example a marker that cannot be merged) degrades to an unlinked circled number instead of a Typst compile error. ## Example ````qmd --- title: "Typst Code Annotations & Filename" format: typst: keep-typ: true code-annotations: true --- ## Filename ```{.r filename="hello.R"} print("Hello, world!") ``` ## Filename and annotations together ```{.r filename="hello.R"} print("Hello, world!") # <1> ``` 1. Greet the world. ## Annotations ```{.python} def greet(name): # <1> msg = f"Hi {name}" # <2> return msg # <3> ``` 1. Define the function. 2. Build the message. 3. Return it. ## One annotation spanning several lines ```{.python} x = 1 # <1> y = 2 # <1> z = x + y # <2> ``` 1. Set the inputs. 2. Compute the sum. ## Cross-referenceable listing ```{#lst-greet .python lst-cap="A greeting function"} print("Hello") # <1> ``` 1. Annotated inside a captioned, referenceable listing. See @lst-greet. ## Identifier containing a dot ```{#lst-a.b .python} x = 1 # <1> ``` 1. Dotted identifiers are valid Pandoc identifiers. ## startFrom ```{.python startFrom="5"} x = 1 # <1> ``` 1. Works whether or not line numbers are displayed. ## startFrom with displayed line numbers ```{.python .number-lines startFrom="5"} x = 1 # <1> ``` 1. The circle follows the code even when numbering starts at 5. ## Fenced echo display block ```{{r}} x <- 1 # <1> ``` 1. The circle lands on the code line, not the fence. ## Annotation without a following list ```{.python} x = 1 # <1> ``` No ordered list follows: the circled number still renders, without a link, instead of failing the render. ```` The same document also renders with `syntax-highlighting: idiomatic` or `none` (native Typst path) and with a light/dark theme object. All behaviours above are covered by smoke-all tests under `tests/docs/smoke-all/typst/code-annotations/` and `tests/docs/smoke-all/typst/code-filename/`.

title: fix(extension): add root guard to dirname loops in extension discovery
description:
## Description

`quarto render` hung when the input file sat at the filesystem root, such as `/mermaid.qmd` in a Docker image with `WORKDIR /`.
Two loops in `src/extension/extension.ts` walk up with `dirname()`, and `dirname("/")` returns `"/"`, so they never ended.

This adds the root guard that `src/project/project-context.ts` already uses to both loops: the extension directory walk in `inputExtensionDirs()` and the brand path lookup in `readExtension()`.

The new unit test calls `inputExtensionDirs()` with the input and the project both at the root.
It runs the call in a Worker with a 10 s timeout, so a missing guard fails the test instead of hanging the suite.
It fails without the fix and passes with it.
The brand loop has no test of its own, because it would need an extension installed at the root.
The test takes the root from `parse(...).root`, so it should reach the guard on Windows too, but I checked that by reading the code, not by running it there.

Closes #14254

title: Honor fig-alt for Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams
description:
## Description

Fixes #3873 and #5514. Also addresses the Mermaid/Graphviz alternative-text propagation reported in #9003 for the output paths below.

Diagram handlers currently discard `fig-alt`: their generated Markdown images have no alternative-text attribute, and their inline SVGs do not receive an accessible name. On unchanged main (`b097576`), the new fixture produces empty DOCX picture descriptions and fails Typst PDF/UA-1 compilation with missing-alt errors for both Mermaid and DOT.

This change:

- Carries `fig-alt` on generated diagram images, preserving `fig-cap`, figure labels, and cross-references.
- Applies an explicit `fig-alt` as the accessible name of inline Mermaid/DOT SVGs, including Mermaid's browser-rendered and prerendered SVG paths. Explicitly empty SVG alt text makes the graphic decorative.
- Leaves native Mermaid accessibility unchanged when `fig-alt` is absent. When an explicit alt overrides `accTitle`, `accDescr` remains available as the accessible description.
- Applies DOCX alternative text after figure layout. Pandoc's DOCX writer uses the image's inline content for `wp:docPr/@descr`, so simply adding an `alt` attribute is insufficient. The late fixup preserves the separate visible caption.
- Adds regression coverage for captioned and uncaptioned diagrams, PNG/SVG output, special characters and Unicode, explicit empty alt in HTML/DOCX, and static-image DOCX captions.

The generic cell-wrapper handling is unchanged. The fix is in the diagram output paths and the DOCX post-layout image fixup.

## Validation

On Windows, using the current main source and its configured Deno 2.7.14, Pandoc 3.10, and Typst 0.15.1:

- **Before the fix:** 10 of the 12 new Chromium checks fail; the two checks preserving native Mermaid accessibility pass. The initial DOCX pictures have empty descriptions, and Typst PDF/UA-1 compilation fails for missing diagram alt text.
- **After the fix:** `diagram-fig-alt.spec.ts --workers=1`: **36/36** pass across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit for HTML and revealjs.
- `tests/unit/core/svg-alt.test.ts`: **3/3** pass.
- Focused smoke tests: **15/15** pass, comprising 8 new HTML/DOCX/Typst render checks plus 7 existing diagram, caption/alignment, GFM, and Typst alt-text regressions. The new Typst fixtures compile with `pdf-standard: ua-1`; DOCX assertions inspect the actual picture-description XML and visible captions.
- `git diff --check` passes. The full Quarto test suite was not run.

The existing R-based Typst regression was run using the installed knitr/rmarkdown packages with `RENV_CONFIG_AUTOLOADER_ENABLED=false`. The SVG DOCX path can emit Pandoc's existing missing-`rsvg-convert` warning on this machine; the embedded SVG's alternative text and caption are verified.

## Review follow-up

@cderv added the following after reviewing the initial change:

- Direct DOCX regression coverage for both a cross-referenced plain image and an ordinary captioned image in `tests/docs/smoke-all/2026/10/16/5514.qmd`, asserting alternative text and preserved visible captions.
- A separate changelog entry for #5514, reflecting that the DOCX fix applies to all images carrying `fig-alt`, not just diagrams.
- Expanded `fig-alt` cell-option format tags to include DOCX, PDF, and Typst, with a format-neutral description, and regenerated editor schema artifacts after merging main.

At head `7962053b36833e7d6781431f467a17ce1e66d548`, all 51 reported PR checks are successful. All five GitHub Actions workflows (Bundle Test, Feature-Format Tests, Parallel Smokes Tests, Test quarto-latexmk, and Performance Check) have completed successfully. The local test counts above describe the original implementation before these follow-up commits.

## Scope

- Native Mermaid code fences in default GFM output are intentionally unchanged; this PR does not replace GitHub's renderer with raster images.
- PPTX's separate Pandoc picture-description behavior is not fixed here.
- In DOCX, explicit `fig-alt=""` preserves an empty picture description but does not set Word's **Mark as decorative** flag. This is not complete decorative-image support; authors currently need to mark such images as decorative in Word after export.
- Existing Typst empty-alt/caption fallback rules are unchanged. The PDF/UA-1 checks exercise diagrams with nonempty alternative text, not a new decorative-image policy.

title: Close hover popups on Esc and when focus leaves them
description:
Footnote, citation, cross-reference and code-annotation popups cannot be dismissed with Esc, and an interactive popup stays open after focus leaves it, covering the next focused element at narrow widths. This fails WCAG 1.4.13 (dismissible) and 2.4.11 (focus not obscured).

## Root cause

The vendored tippy.js 6.3.7 has no Esc handling. Its focusout listener sits only on the trigger, so with `interactive: true` focus moving into the popup is ignored and nothing notices focus leaving it afterwards.

## Fix

A tippy plugin, wired into both the `tippyHover` and the code-annotation configs, listens while a popup is shown:

- Esc hides the popup. If focus is inside it, focus returns to the trigger, with the instance disabled meanwhile so the focus trigger does not reopen it.
- focusout from the popup to an element outside both popup and trigger hides it. A null `relatedTarget` is ignored, so clicking non-focusable text inside the popup keeps it open.

A few cases needed more than the sketch in the issue:

- Cross-reference popups call `show()` from `onTrigger`, ahead of tippy's own 100ms delayed show, which reopened the popup right after Esc. Pending delay timeouts are now cleared before hiding.
- With `code-annotations: select` the trigger is `click`, and tippy has no blur handling for it. The trigger's focusout now closes the popup, and cancels a pending show when focus leaves within the 50 ms delay.
- In revealjs, Esc is also bound to the slide overview. The keydown listener runs in the capture phase and stops propagation so Esc only closes the popup. It still propagates when the slide menu is open and handles keys itself, so a single Esc reaches the menu. A menu with `keyboard: false` handles nothing, so propagation requires keyboard handling to be on.

`tippyOptions.config` cannot override plugins: it is serialized with `JSON.stringify` and only set internally (revealjs offset and maxWidth).

The Playwright tests cover the four popup types in HTML, select mode, and revealjs. The `tabUntilFocused` helper was copied into four specs and the WebKit Alt+Tab mapping inlined in three more, so both now live in `src/utils.ts`.

Fixes #15080

title: Add DOCX figure caption and alt text baseline tests
description:
#15077 changes how `fig-alt` reaches DOCX: a late fixup in `quarto-post/docx.lua` rewrites each image's inline content so Pandoc writes it as the picture description (`wp:docPr/@descr`). Its tests cover diagrams, one captioned image and one cross-referenced image. Nothing currently pins the visible caption for the other ways an image ends up in a DOCX document, so it is hard to check that the fixup only changes `descr`.

These smoke-all tests go to main first. Then main gets merged into #15077, and CI has to stay green on that branch with them.

They assert the visible caption text for:

- plain figure, cross-referenced figure, subfigure panel, div float, non-crossref `layout-ncol`
- linked image, image in a table cell, image in a callout, rich caption, special characters in `fig-alt`
- knitr and Jupyter cells: cross-ref, unlabelled, `fig-subcap` layout

Every alt value includes an `ALT-ONLY` marker, and the tests check that this marker never shows up in the document text. For `descr`, only the values that must stay the same are asserted: images without `fig-alt` (the caption for a plain figure, empty for a cross-referenced one and for the callout icon). The `descr` values that #15077 changes on purpose will get assertions on its branch after the merge.

Caption text is compared with `string-join(.//w:t, '')` and not with `normalize-space(.)`. fontoxpath's `normalize-space` turns the non-breaking space after "Figure" into a regular space, and cross-ref caption paragraphs have extra whitespace-only text nodes.

Related to #15077

title: Warn and ignore a brand file that holds only comments
description:
## Description

Fixes #14891.

A `_brand.yml` that is all comments parses to no YAML value, so the brand schema rejects it with `YAML value is missing` and the render stops. Both loaders in `projectResolveBrand` now check for an empty value first, print a warning (once per file) and carry on as if the file wasn't there. What I checked on Windows 11:

- `brand: my-brand.yml` in front matter pointing at a comment-only file: warning, renders
- `brand: {light, dark}` with a comment-only dark file: warning, the light brand is still applied
- a normal brand file still applies (colour shows up in the compiled CSS)

The new smoke-all test (`2026/10/13/issue-14891`) fails without the change and passes with it, and the existing brand tests (126 documents, 197 checks) pass.

One thing I noticed along the way but left out of this PR: a brand file with broken YAML, e.g. an unclosed `[`, fails with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'value')` rather than a validation message. That happens on `main` too. Happy to open a separate issue for it.

title: Fix page-level website option validation and social metadata opt-out
description:
Website pages read several `website` options from their own front matter, but the document schema did not declare some of them, and a page `open-graph: false` did not opt the page out. Follow-up to #15084, which did the same declaration work for page-level `open-graph` and `twitter-card`.

## Page-level navigation options

`bread-crumbs`, `back-to-top-navigation`, `page-navigation`, `margin-header` and `margin-footer` are read from page front matter, and the website navigation docs show the first three set per page. They were only declared under `website:`, so a page value of the wrong type passed validation silently and editors offered no completion.

They are now declared in `document-website.yml` with the same types as their `website:` counterparts. Descriptions follow the page-level behavior: the three booleans only opt a page out (`page-navigation: true` also opts in), and page margin headers and footers are added after the site ones.

## Social metadata opt-out

With `open-graph: true` or `twitter-card: true` under `website:`, a page setting the same option to `false`, in its front matter or in a `_metadata.yml`, still got `og:` or `twitter:` tags. The provider loop in `website-meta.ts` skipped a provider only when both the page and site values were falsy, and the merge of site and page options treats a page `false` like an unset value, so the site value won.

A page `false` now skips the provider, as a page `false` already does for `page-navigation`, `bread-crumbs`, `back-to-top-navigation` and `search`. An empty page value (`open-graph:` with nothing after it) still falls back to the site settings.

Documentation of the page opt-out: quarto-dev/quarto-web#2297

title: Fix shortcodes in math not resolved when they are the only shortcodes
description:
## Description

Closes #15092. Follow-up to #14279.

The shortcode filter only runs when `compute_flags()` sets `flags.has_shortcodes`. `compute_flags()` looked for shortcodes in `Shortcode`, `Code`, `RawInline`, `RawBlock`, `CodeBlock`, `Link`, `Image` and attributes, but not in `Math` nodes. This adds a `Math` handler to `compute_flags()` (same check as for `Code`).

The existing `shortcode-math.qmd` test from #14279 also contains a shortcode outside math, which sets the flag and hid this case. The new test `shortcode-math-only.qmd` has shortcodes only in inline and display math and checks HTML and LaTeX output.

title: Install hyphenation patterns missing for babel .ini locales
description:
With `babeloptions: provide=*` (or `\babelprovide[import]{...}` in a header), babel sets the document language up from its `.ini` file. When the hyphenation patterns are not installed, it falls back to the current `\language` and only logs an Info line. The PDF renders without a warning, hyphenated with English patterns, and nothing gets installed.

This is the Quarto side of rstudio/tinytex#522 (fixes rstudio/tinytex#519), which exports the maps behind the detection as `babel-hyphen.json` in the daily `regex.tar.gz`. It is written as if that file is published, so it stays a draft until #522 is merged and a daily release carries the file.

## Why lookup maps are needed

The same pair of Info lines is logged for legitimate locales whose patterns were found under another name (`austrian` set to `\l@ngerman-x-2024-02-28`, `canadianfrench` set to `\l@french`). A fallback can only be told apart by comparing the target with the hyphenation language the locale's `.ini` file expects, modulo language.dat synonyms.

## Fix

`detectBabelFallback()` follows `detect_babel_fallback()` in tinytex and its result is merged with the warning-based detection in `findMissingHyphenationFiles()`, so the missing package goes through the existing install and retry path. `babel-hyphen.json` is a verbatim copy of the tinytex file, imported statically so it is inlined into the bundle. The `\l@nil` check is removed since it is the same fallback, and `chinese` still resolves to nothing as before (#10291).

The Importing regex is the one from rstudio/tinytex#522. It pairs only the `data` and `basic data` levels, and accepts the unquoted language name that babel 3.84 writes. Languages loaded from an `.ldf` file log the identification-only level and then register their own dialect patterns (`\l@ngerman`), so pairing them would make `lang: de-AT` and `lang: de-CH` install `dehyph-exptl` on every render.

The daily `verify-tinytex-patterns.yml` check now tracks `babel-hyphen.json` like `hyphen.json`. The first scheduled run after this merges reports it as having no cached version and opens one review issue with the whole file, which is the expected baseline.

Fixes #15082

title: Validate page-level open-graph and twitter-card options
description:
Follow-up to #15057, whose `image` description now sends users to page-level `open-graph` to declare the preview image size.

Page front matter `open-graph` and `twitter-card` are read by the website metadata postprocessor and merged with the `website:` options, as the [website tools guide](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-tools.html) documents. The schema only declared them under `website:`, so at page level they got no validation and no editor completion. A misspelled option such as `imge-width` was silently ignored, and a value of the wrong type such as `description: 42` crashed the render with `TypeError: value.trim is not a function`. The same mistakes under `website:` in `_quarto.yml` are reported with a "Did you mean" hint.

## Fix

Declare both keys in `document-website.yml`, reusing `open-graph-config` and `twitter-card-config`, so a page accepts the same options as the website. An empty value (`open-graph:` with nothing after it) is accepted too: the postprocessor handles it, and the #12016 tests rely on it.

> [!NOTE]
> A page or `_metadata.yml` with an unknown option under `open-graph` or `twitter-card` used to render, with the option ignored. It now fails validation, as it already does under `website:`. The changelog entry says so.

The tests validate front matter strings against the real schema in a unit test, not with a smoke-all document per value, so another case is one more table row. The testing guidance in `llm-docs/testing-patterns.md` and `.claude/rules/` now points schema changes to this kind of test. These tests load the generated `yaml-intelligence-resources.json`, not the `.yml` source, so `dev-call build-artifacts` has to run before they see a schema change.

The quarto.org format reference is generated from this schema, so it will list both options for pages at the next reference update.

title: Fix twitter-card image size tags and options
description:
Follow-up to #15083, from the same pass over the `image-*` options.

With `site-url` set, the size Quarto measures from a local PNG or JPEG image was written to every social metadata provider. The twitter provider passed it through as `twitter:image-height` and `twitter:image-width`, which are not Twitter Card tags: Twitter Cards define only `twitter:image` and `twitter:image:alt` for images. The PNG case dates back to 2021, and #15050 extended it to JPEG. Crawlers ignore unknown meta names, so the impact is cosmetic. The measured size now goes to `og:image:height` and `og:image:width` only.

The `twitter-card` `image-width` and `image-height` options come from the same mix-up (#12014). `twitter-card` shared its options with `open-graph`, so the two showed in the reference although nothing reads them. They move to `open-graph`. On `twitter-card` they stay accepted as hidden options, since it is a closed object and removing them would turn a harmless no-op into a failed render for any config that sets them. Setting them prints a warning that they are ignored and points to `open-graph`, without announcing a removal.

The #15050 changelog entry no longer claims `twitter:image` gets a height and width.

title: Install dehyph-exptl for pinned German hyphenation patterns
description:
Follow-up to #15029 (fix for #15027). The hyphenation table in `parse-error.ts` was a hand-written copy of the one in tinytex and had drifted. tinytex now generates it from `texlive.tlpdb` and exports it as `hyphen.json` (rstudio/tinytex#517, follow-up to rstudio/tinytex#516).

With `\begin{hyphenrules}{ngerman-x-latest}` and no dehyph-exptl installed, babel stops with `You haven't defined the language 'ngerman-x-latest' yet`. The map held suffixes and the package was always built as `hyphen-<name>`, so tlmgr was asked for the non-existent `hyphen-ngerman-x-latest` and the render failed. The package that provides these patterns is `dehyph-exptl`.

## Fix

Detection now follows tinytex `main` (`hyphen_pkgs()`, `check_babel()`, `detect_hyphen()`, `check_polyglossia()` in `R/latex.R`):

- `kHyphenationPackageNames` holds full package names and has the 41 entries of tinytex's `hyphen.json`, including the 4 `dehyph-exptl` ones. The language name is validated (`^[a-z0-9-]+$`) instead of the resulting package name.
- A language given as a description keeps its first word, so `German (current orthography)` gives `hyphen-german`.
- The babel regex only reads warning blocks, as tinytex's `latex_warning()` does, instead of matching any `(babel)` line once a babel warning exists.
- Every warned language is returned, not only the first, and `Package polyglossia Warning: No hyphenation patterns were loaded` is detected. Packages are deduplicated and installed together, so an extra language no longer costs one more compilation.
- `verify-tinytex-patterns.yml` also compares `hyphen.json`, so the existing `tinytex-patterns` issue reports changes to the map. The cache key changes: the first run after merge sets a new baseline for both files and opens no issue. When the daily release can't be downloaded, the run reports the comparison as skipped (warning and summary) instead of "No changes detected", and nothing is cached.

The `chinese` skip list (#10291), the `Hyphen rules for '...' set to \l@nil` fallback and unquoted names in the babel error regex only exist here and are kept.

Out of scope, tracked in rstudio/tinytex#518 and left for Quarto to follow after tinytex: `\babelprovide[hyphenrules=...]` warnings, `hyphsubst` "Unknown pattern" errors, and the Swiss German (1901) mapping to `hyphen-swiss`.

A document with `lang: de` and `ngerman-x-latest`, rendered with the dev build without dehyph-exptl installed, now logs `installing dehyph-exptl` and produces the PDF.

Fixes #15035

title: Remove never-read top-level image-width and image-height options
description:
The document schema declares top-level `image-width` and `image-height`, and the `image` description says they size the Twitter Card preview. No code path has ever read them. Open Graph sizes come from `open-graph: image-width/image-height` or from measuring the image file, as #15040 already notes.

The keys were added to the schema in 2021 (`e8da14211`). The only reads in history were scoped to the Open Graph and Twitter providers, and the Twitter ones were removed in `07378ec24`. No top-level read has existed on `main`, so removing the keys changes no rendered output.

Because the schema types them as strings, a numeric value such as `image-width: 1200` is rejected by schema validation, for an option that does nothing.

## Fix

Remove both entries from `document-website.yml`. Document front matter accepts undeclared keys, so numeric and string values now render and are ignored. The `image` description points to `open-graph` for declaring the preview image size.

Wiring them up instead was not chosen. The same name already sets the about-page image width (`about` options, `website-about.ts:42`), so reusing it at the top level would be ambiguous. quarto-web already documents that top-level page values "aren't used" (quarto-dev/quarto-web#2282).

Declared `twitter-card` `image-width` and `image-height` have not been read since 2021 either; when `site-url` is set, Quarto instead emits the measured image size as `twitter:image-height`/`twitter:image-width`. This PR does not change either.

The quarto.org format reference is generated from this schema, so it stops listing options that have no effect at the next reference update.

Related to #12016

title: Fix website og:image using a data URI image joined to site-url
description:
When a website page sets no `image`, `og:image` and `twitter:image` can end up as a data URI joined to `site-url`, like `https://example.com/data:image/png;base64,...`. The ORCID badge rendered in the title block for an author with an `orcid` is the common trigger. Since #15050 reads the size of any image path, the same page now fails to render on `main` with a `stat` error on the data URI. The crash is not in a release, the wrong URL is older.

## Root cause

Two places treat a data URI as a file path:

1. Preview image discovery in `discover-meta.ts` returns it. The check added in 2023 to not test data URIs against the named file regex returns them instead of skipping them, and the last resort pass only excludes `http`/`https` images.
2. Image resolution (`imageMetadata`, `projectRelativeHref`) only special-cases absolute URLs, so a data URI is resolved as a project path and joined to `site-url`. Listing items using `projectRelativeHref` got `/posts/data:...` the same way.

## Fix

Crawlers and feed readers fetch these images by URL, so a data URI can't be used there:

- Discovery for social metadata skips data URIs and moves on to the next image of the page, then the site `image`. Every image marked `.preview-image` is now tried, not only the first one.
- A data URI set explicitly as a page, site, listing item or feed `image` is ignored with a warning for social metadata and listing feeds, and the next candidate is used.
- `projectRelativeHref` leaves data URIs as is. Listing cards are displayed by the browser, so they keep showing them.

Fixes #15055

title: Move the OJS runtime and its Observable forks from quarto-dev/quarto
description:
Closes #15043.

This moves the OJS runtime and its vendored Observable forks from quarto-dev/quarto's `packages/ojs/` into `packages/ojs/` here, next to `packages/quarto-types`. It adds an npm build that regenerates the committed bundles, and a CI check that the committed bundles match the sources. quarto-dev/quarto#1180 deletes the copy there once this lands.

## Commits

Each commit is reviewable separately:

1. **Copy `packages/ojs` from quarto-dev/quarto.** A verbatim copy from quarto-dev/quarto@42177e13, the commit before #1180's deletion, so #1180's rollup tooling upgrade comes along. The only file left out is `quarto-ojs-runtime/assets/quarto.css`, because this repo's `quarto-ojs.css` is newer.
2. **Build with npm.** The changes to the copied files:
   - `packages/ojs/package.json` is an npm workspace root that links the runtime and the five forks. It has a committed `package-lock.json`. `npm run build` writes `quarto-ojs-runtime{,.min}.js` straight into `src/resources/formats/html/ojs/`.
   - The forks' `devDependencies` and `yarn.lock` files are removed. They were only for each fork's own build and tests, which never ran in quarto-dev/quarto's CI either. Their old rollup plugins fail npm's peer dependency checks (`rollup-plugin-terser` 7 needs rollup 2, but the forks use rollup 3), and they would keep the dev-only Snyk advisories.
   - The compiler fork's `package.json` gets `"module": "src/index.js"`. Its `main` was a UMD `dist/` that had to be built first with rollup 1. Now the runtime's rollup bundles the compiler from its ES module source. This also makes `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` unnecessary: with it removed, the output is byte-identical.
   - The banner no longer includes `new Date().getFullYear()`, so a rebuild gives the same bytes in any year. The banner used to read "Copyright 2024 undefined"; now it reads `// quarto-ojs-runtime v0.0.19 Copyright Posit Software, PBC`. The runtime's version is bumped to 0.0.19.
   - `notes.md` is replaced with a `README.md`. The old notes' `git subtree pull` commands won't work on plain copies.
3. **Rebuild the bundles and check them in CI.** This adds `.github/workflows/test-ojs-runtime.yml`, which runs when `packages/ojs/**` or the bundles change. It runs `npm ci && npm run build`, then fails if `git diff` shows the bundles changed.

## Bundle changes

Compared with #1180's bundle, the new one differs only in how the compiler is included. The compiler's code is inlined as ES modules instead of as an embedded UMD blob, which also renumbers some identifiers (`hasOwnProperty$2` → `$3`, and so on). The bundled library versions are the same: acorn 7.4.1 for the compiler's `@observablehq/parser` 4.2, and acorn 8.17.0 for the parser fork.

Compared with the bundle on `main`, which was last rebuilt in 2024-02, this also ships everything listed in #15043: acorn 8.8.1 → 8.17, the `debugger` removal, inspector 5.0.1, Inputs 0.10.6, and mime 4 (`FileAttachment(…).mimeType` is `text/javascript` for `.js`). `@observablehq/inputs` stays on 0.10, as the README notes.

## Testing

- `npm ci && npm run build` in `packages/ojs` on Node 24 / npm 11: clean install, 0 vulnerabilities, no peer warnings. Rebuilding from a fresh `npm ci` reproduces the committed bundles exactly.
- I rendered all of `tests/docs/playwright/ojs/*.qmd` with the dev build and ran the 7 OJS spec files (9 tests) in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: 27/27 pass. The rendered pages load the v0.0.19 bundle.

## Notes for reviewers

- I didn't preserve history (`git subtree`/`filter-repo`), because PRs here are squash-merged. The source commit is recorded in commit 1 and in the README.
- The forks' nested `.github/` and `.circleci/` directories came along with the copy. They're inactive outside the repo root. I kept them so the forks stay close to upstream.
- `deno lint`/`fmt` only include `src/`, so they don't check the vendored JS.

title: Move navbar search after nav links so tab order matches visual order
description:
## Description

Closes #7058.

In a collapsible navbar, the search control (`#quarto-search`) came second in the DOM, right after the brand. CSS flex `order` places it visually at the far right. So keyboard and screen-reader users reached Search before the navigation links: brand → **Search** → Home → About → tools. The recommended way to make focus order match visual order is to align the DOM with it ([WCAG technique C27](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C27)).

This PR moves the `navsearch.ejs` partial to the end of the collapse branch in `nav-before-body.ejs`, after the nav links and tools. The other two branches (non-collapse, no nav items) already emit search last. Tab order becomes: brand → nav links → tools → **Search**.

**No visual change.** Every navbar child has a distinct CSS `order` at every breakpoint (`quarto-nav.scss`, `quarto-search.scss`), so DOM order never decides layout. Checks done:

- Headless-Chrome screenshots at 1400px and 500px are byte-identical to a render without this change.
- Element geometry is identical with the mobile menu collapsed and expanded, and with `tools-collapse: true`.
- The search div stays a sibling of `#navbarCollapse`, outside the collapse region, so it stays visible at small widths.

**Possible downstream effects** (noted in the changelog):

- Custom CSS or JS that expects `#quarto-search` before the nav links in the DOM (for example, sibling selectors) needs an update.
- Custom themes that set two `$navbar-*-order` variables to the same value: a tie now resolves with search later. Stock themes have no ties.

Nothing in quarto-cli depends on the old position: `quarto-search.js` finds the div with `getElementById`, and no test or stylesheet uses structural selectors on the navbar.

**Tests:** the new smoke-all test `tests/docs/smoke-all/website/navbar-search-order/` asserts `#navbarCollapse ~ #quarto-search` and `.quarto-navbar-tools ~ #quarto-search`, and rejects the reverse orderings. It fails against the old template. All `smoke/site/` and `smoke/website/` tests pass (50), plus the `website` and `website-search` smoke-all documents (21).

title: Resolve website images through one shared helper
description:
Follow-up to #15053 and #15032. The listing feed image size lookup missed the `project.dir` join (#15032) because the same resolve-and-size logic was written by hand in three places, and the per-item copy had the join while the feed-level copy did not. #15053 settled which base each image source resolves against and moved the path half into `projectRelativeHref`. The URL check, the project join and the `imageSize` call were still repeated.

`resolveProjectImage(image, projectDir, documentDir)` in `website-shared.ts` now does all three: it builds the project relative href with `projectRelativeHref`, skips the size lookup for web URLs (a URL joined onto a Windows path makes `stat` throw, #15022), and reads the size from the project file otherwise. The feed-level image, the per-item feed image and `imageMetadata` call it.

URL building stays at the call sites, `absoluteUrl` for feeds and `joinUrl` for page metadata. The helper adds no error handling, so `imageSize` read and decode errors propagate as before. `imageMetadata` drops its `path` field, which nothing read.

The one output change is in the feeds. Relative paths now go through `join` like page metadata images already did, so `./feed.png` gives `https://example.com/feed.png` instead of `https://example.com/./feed.png`, and `img//feed.png` gives `/img/feed.png`. Paths starting with `/` keep their href as written. Images outside the project are not supported input and have no handling.

`render-listing-feed-image` gains a local per-item image in its fixture (`image: ../feed.png`) and asserts its `media:content`. Per-item local images had no rendered check, and that assertion passes on the base commit as well.

title: Fix relative og:image and feed image paths for subdirectory pages
description:
For a page in a subdirectory, a relative image path used for `og:image`, `twitter:image` and the listing feed resolves against the wrong directory. With `website: image: site.png` in `_quarto.yml` and `site.png` at the project root, `blog/index.qmd` gets the `og:image` `https://example.com/blog/site.png`, a file that does not exist, and no width or height. A listing page `news/index.qmd` with `image: thumb.png` (the file is in `news/`) gets the feed `<image><url>` `https://example.com/thumb.png`, also without a size.

## Root cause

Each source was resolved against one fixed base, whatever file it was written in:

- The `website.image` fallback was added for #5389 without a base decision, and `imageMetadata` resolves any relative path against the rendering document.
- `website: open-graph: image:` and `website: twitter-card: image:` are merged into each page's metadata, so the information that they come from `_quarto.yml` is lost.
- The feed reads every image as project relative, but the page `image` is documented as relative to the document.

## Fix

An image path is relative to the file it is written in:

- `website: image:`, `website: open-graph: image:` and `website: twitter-card: image:` in `_quarto.yml` are relative to the project. Quarto rebases the other paths of `_quarto.yml` to each document, but `website:` is excluded because its paths are project relative.
- A page `image:`, a page `open-graph:` or `twitter-card:` `image:`, and the same keys from `_metadata.yml` are relative to the document.
- `feed: image:` stays relative to the project, like `xml-stylesheet` in the same block. The schema description now says so.

Paths starting with `/` and URLs are unchanged. Without `site-url` the value is written as is, as before.

A site image is turned into its leading-`/` form before it reaches the page metadata, so the existing project relative branch gives the URL and the size, and registers the file as a page resource (a `website.image` used only by subdirectory pages is still copied to the output). That branch built the URL by concatenation, which doubled the slash when `site-url` ends with `/`, so it now uses `joinUrl`. The merge of site and page metadata also stopped writing the page image into the site object shared by all pages.

For the feed, the page `image` of a listing is joined onto the listing's directory. The helper doing this is the one the listing item images already used, moved to `website-shared.ts` as `projectRelativeHref`.

Alternative considered: making `website.image` document relative was rejected, since the schema describes it as the site thumbnail and it only works from a single base.

## Existing sites

A sample of public sites found through GitHub code search suggests few relative values would change meaning:

- `website: image:`: 0 of 58 sites break, and about 43 get a working `og:image` on subdirectory pages.
- Site-level `open-graph` / `twitter-card` `image:`: 0 of 17 break.
- Page `image` used as the feed image on subdirectory listings: 20 of 27 are fixed. 3 worked by accident and change, and their `og:image` was already broken.

Related to #15040, which edits the same block of `website-meta.ts` to keep a declared image size. A companion documentation PR for quarto-web will be linked here.

Fixes #15039

title: Never reuse an existing Playwright fixture server
description:
Follow-up to #15013, which made the Playwright fixture server port configurable with `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT`.

When another process already answers on the fixture port, a local Playwright run uses it as its fixture server without checking what it serves. With two worktrees running Playwright at the same time, the second run tests the first worktree's rendered `tests/docs/playwright` HTML: a spec passed locally with its own rendered fixture deleted. An unrelated app answering 200 on the port makes every spec fail on missing elements instead, which looks like a regression in the feature under test.

## Root cause

`playwright.config.ts` sets `reuseExistingServer: !isCI` on the fixture server. Locally, Playwright then reuses any server whose `/` answers with a status from 200 to 403. CI is not affected, as `CI` is set there and reuse was already off.

## Fix

The fixture server is never reused. A busy port now fails the run at once with Playwright's `http://127.0.0.1:<port> is already used` error, and each concurrent run sets its own `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT`. Nothing starts the fixture server ahead of a run, so reuse only ever applied to this collision case; the cost is starting the server on each run (about 1.4 s on Windows).

The revealjs multiplex server keeps `reuseExistingServer: !isCI`. It starts on every run whatever specs are selected, and its port 1948 is fixed in `revealjs/multiplex.qmd`, so turning reuse off for it made any second concurrent run fail, even on its own fixture port. It serves no test fixtures, so sharing it cannot make a run test another checkout's HTML.

A process answering 404 on the fixture port is still not detected as busy: Playwright starts its own `http.server`, which on Windows binds over the occupied port, and the run times out after 120 s. That case never runs tests against the wrong content, so it is only documented in the Playwright testing rules.

## Test plan

Local only, as CI keeps its current behavior:

- [x] Free port: `html-callouts.spec.ts` passes
- [x] Another `python -m http.server 8765` serving a copy of the rendered fixture: the run stops at once with `already used` (before: 3 passed with the local fixture deleted)
- [x] Another run holding 8765 and 1948, this run with `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=8766`: passes, including `revealjs-multiplex.spec.ts`
- [x] No server left listening after passing and failing runs

title: Fix callout title option rendered as HTML title attribute
description:
While working on #15041, I noticed that a callout's `title` option also ends up as an HTML `title` attribute: on the `.callout` div in html, and on the wrapper div in revealjs and epub. Browsers show it as a tooltip over the whole callout, repeating the heading already displayed.

The callout parser in `src/resources/filters/customnodes/callout.lua` reads `title` but does not remove it from the div attributes, unlike `appearance`, `collapse` and `icon` next to it. `title` is now removed once read. Other leftover attributes like `data-*` still pass through.

In revealjs and epub, a callout with an id and a title no longer gets a wrapper div, as no leftover attributes remain. It renders as a single div, like an untitled callout with an id since #15041.
