title: Keep declared open-graph image size for images Quarto cannot measure
description:
With `site-url` set, `og:image:width` and `og:image:height` disappear for an `open-graph` image that Quarto cannot measure, even when `image-width` and `image-height` are declared. #12016 reported it for a JPEG, which #15050 now measures. The remaining cases are remote images and formats Quarto does not read, such as SVG, GIF or WebP.

## Root cause

`resolveImageMetadata` in `src/project/types/website/website-meta.ts` always replaced the declared size with the measured one, which is `undefined` when the image can't be measured. Without `site-url` this code is skipped, which is why removing `site-url` hides the problem.

## Fix

The measured size is still used when Quarto can read the file, so the tags describe the actual pixels. Otherwise the declared size is kept.

Keeping the declared size raises the question of which image it describes. A size declared in the site `open-graph` options describes the site image, so it no longer applies when the page supplies its own image: `image`, a page `open-graph` `image`, or a preview image found in the page content. That image only gets the dimensions declared in the page `open-graph` options, each one separately. `image: false` and the `website.image` fallback keep the site image and its size.

## Compatibility

This changes the output of sites without `site-url`. Before, the site-declared size was emitted on every page, including pages with their own image. A site that declared one size because all its page images share it now loses these tags on pages that set an image.

The check is on whether the page declares an image, not on which file it is, so a page that repeats the site image also loses the site size.

To keep the tags, declare `image-width` and `image-height` under `open-graph` in the page front matter, or once in shared metadata such as `_metadata.yml`. Top-level `image-width` and `image-height` in the page front matter are not read for `open-graph`.

Fixes #12016

title: Fix revealjs and epub callout id rendered on two divs
description:
In revealjs and EPUB output, a callout with an id renders that id on two nested divs:

```html
<div id="my-id" title="Titled">
<div id="my-id" class="callout callout-note callout-titled callout-style-default">
```

Duplicate ids are invalid HTML. `getElementById()` returns only the outer div, and a CSS `#my-id` rule applies to both (doubled borders, margins, padding). HTML output is not affected: the bootstrap renderer emits a single `.callout` div.

## Root cause

The revealjs/epub renderer wraps the `.callout` div in an outer div so leftover classes such as `.fragment` survive (#5208, #6853). The wrapper was created whenever the callout had an id, and it received the full attribute set, identifier included. When cross-referenceable callouts were added (a0a7b4a2f, first released in v1.4.458), the inner `.callout` div started carrying the id as well, so both divs have it. Reproduced on released 1.4.549 and v1.9.38, and on current main.

## Fix

The id stays on the `.callout` div, the same element as in HTML output, so `.callout#x` selectors behave the same across formats. The wrapper is now created only when classes or attributes are left over, and it gets a copy of the attributes without the identifier. An id-only callout renders as a single div.

Alternative considered: keeping the id on the wrapper and blanking the inner one. This was rejected because the id would no longer be on the `.callout` element, and `.callout#x` (used in the existing `revealjs-callouts.spec.ts` locators) would stop matching.

This changes what `#x` selects in revealjs and EPUB, so it targets 1.11 without a backport. Selectors such as `#x > .callout` or `getElementById('x').querySelector('.callout')` no longer match, and neither works in HTML. Reveal fragment-event code keyed on `event.fragment.id` for `{#x .callout-note .fragment}` is affected too, since `.fragment` stays on the wrapper.

The `title` attribute still leaks onto the wrapper as an HTML attribute, which keeps titled callouts wrapped. That is separate from this fix.

## Test plan

- [x] `div.callout#…` selectors and absence of `[id=x] [id=x]` in the new smoke-all document, reverse-applying the fix gives an assertion failure
- [x] `6853.qmd` (fragment wrapper) still passes
- [x] EPUB: unzip the rendered `.epub` and `grep -rhn 'id="my-id\|id="other' EPUB/text/` shows one line per id, each on `class="callout …"`

Fixes #15036

title: Support JPEG image sizes for feed and open-graph metadata
description:
`imageSize()` only measured PNG files, and only when the path ended in a lowercase `.png`. A JPEG feed image, listing item image or `og:image` therefore never got a height or width: no `<height>`/`<width>` in the feed `<image>`, no size on item `media:content`, no `og:image:width`/`og:image:height`. JPEG is the common format for photo thumbnails, and #12016 showed users do need the open-graph sizes for them.

`imageSize()` now picks the parser from the file's header bytes instead of its extension. This also fixes `feed.PNG`, `.jpeg` and `.jfif` paths, which the extension check skipped. JPEG sizes come from a new `src/core/jpeg.ts` that scans markers up to the first start-of-frame segment, with no new dependency. Baseline and progressive JPEGs are both read. Callers are unchanged.

Only PNG and JPEG are measured. SVG often has no pixel size, and Facebook and X reject SVG `og:image` anyway. GIF, WebP and AVIF can be added the same way if there is demand. Unknown formats still return `undefined`, as before.

`png.ts` now exports `isPng()`, which checks the 8-byte signature from the PNG spec. It replaces the old check that compared the bytes joined as decimal digits against the string `"13780787113102610"`.

Related to #15040, which fixes the same open-graph size behaviour for declared sizes with `site-url`.

title: Fix listing contents files resolved against the working directory
description:
A file named next to a folder in a listing's `contents`, like `contents: [posts, archived-items.yaml]` from the "YAML Listing Content" docs, is dropped when the site is rendered from a directory other than the listing page's. If a file with the same name exists in the working directory, that one is listed instead. A `.qmd` named next to its own folder is listed twice.

It works by accident in the usual layout, a listing page at the project root rendered from the root. With the page in a subdirectory, which is what CI and `quarto render` from the root do, the YAML items silently disappear.

## Root cause

When `contents` mixes a folder (or the default glob) with a file, `filterPaths` only matches project input documents. A follow-up loop in `filterListingFiles` then adds entries that name an existing non-input file such as YAML. That loop checked existence and joined the path against `Deno.cwd()`, and `isAbsolute` read an anchored `/items.yml` as the filesystem root. It also never checked for files `filterPaths` had already included. A lone `contents: items.yml` goes through `resolvePathGlobs(dirname(source))` and was already correct.

The loop has resolved against the cwd since it was added in 4ad0f0004. #15032 fixed the same class of problem for the listing feed image.

## Fix

Each entry is resolved against the listing document's directory first, as the lone-entry form and the docs do. A real absolute path still works as a fallback. `!` exclusions, the listing document itself and files already included are skipped.

An anchored `/items.yml` next to a folder now means the listing directory, like the lone form, instead of the filesystem root.

`!` exclusions are not applied to files this loop adds. That was already the case and is unchanged here.

Fixes #15044

title: Fix revealjs screen reader fragment announcements
description:
Fixes #15019.

## Description

Backport the not-yet-merged hakimel/reveal.js#3946 to the bundled reveal.js 5.1.0 without upgrading to 6.x.

Hidden incremental content is excluded from `.aria-status` until it is revealed, including nested fragments and pauses. Fragment text is computed and announced only after all fragment classes are updated, so backward navigation uses the final visibility of nested normal and fade-out fragments. The fragment itself can still be announced when activated, and the built-in initially visible and transient styles retain their behavior.

URL handling no longer navigates back to the current slide or fragment after writing its own history entry. Named horizontal slide indices are normalized, explicit fragment links still work, and browser Back can return to the state before the first fragment when `fragment-in-url` is enabled.

The readable source patch is retained in `package/src/common/patches/` and reapplied by the HTML dependency updater before rebuilding both JavaScript bundles and source maps. Before removing this backport, check that the upstream PR has landed in the release being bundled.

## Validation

- Eight Playwright scenarios cover actual live-region mutation counts, nested normal and fade-out fragments in both directions, pauses, fragment URLs, and browser Back/Forward.
- 24/24 checks pass across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. The four new backward-navigation cases fail against the previous PR bundle on Chromium and pass after this revision.
- Rebuilt the UMD and ESM bundles from 5.1.0. The source maps contain source changes only in `js/reveal.js`, `js/controllers/location.js`, and `js/controllers/fragments.js`. The readable patch applies cleanly to pristine 5.1.0 and reproduces these sources.
- Local fixture rendering used Quarto 1.8.27, with the rebuilt bundles and current support plugin copied into the output before testing. The full Quarto build and test suite were not run.

title: Fix revealjs callout spacing below a final code block
description:
When a code block is the last element of a callout in Revealjs, it sits against the bottom of the callout since 1.8.15. With `appearance="simple"` and no title, the code block border touches the callout border.

## Root cause

Since #13024, code blocks are wrapped in a `div.code-copy-outer-scaffold` for the copy button, and Revealjs uses the same HTML postprocessor. Two rules added in #11251 for a code block in last position select `div.sourceCode` as the last child of `.callout-content`, so they no longer match:

- In titled callouts, the last child gets `padding-bottom: 0.5rem` and no margin, except a `div.sourceCode`. The scaffold is not excluded, so it gets the 8px padding instead of the 12px block margin.
- In simple untitled callouts, a last `div.sourceCode` gets `margin-bottom: 1rem`. This rule never matches now.

## Fix

It has no padding or border, so the spacing is the same as in 1.7.34 (12px in titled callouts, 16px in simple untitled ones). The `:not()` uses a selector list, so the specificity of the titled rule doesn't change. The `div.sourceCode` selectors are kept for `code-copy: false`, where there is no scaffold.

title: Fix listing feed image size depending on the render directory
description:
When a website project is rendered from outside its directory (`quarto render path/to/project`), the listing feed `<image>` silently loses its `<height>` and `<width>`. Rendering the same project from inside its directory keeps them. A feed image written with a leading `/` (`image: /feed.png`) never gets them, whatever the directory.

Found while reviewing #15026, but the bug predates it.

## Root cause

`createFeed` passes the feed image (listing `feed: image:`, the document `image`, or the site `image`) unchanged to `imageSize()` in `website-listing-feed.ts`, so a relative path is read from the current working directory instead of the project. The feed `<url>` for the same image is built project-relative with `absoluteUrl()`, and per-item images in the same file already join `project.dir` before reading their size.

## Fix

The size is now read from `join(project.dir, image)`, the same project file the feed `<url>` points at. Rendering from the project directory gives the same output as before.

The new smoke test renders a fixture project from the `tests/` directory and checks the size for the listing option, the site `image` fallback and a leading `/` path.

title: Fix notebook preview header hidden by website header
description:
On a website with a navbar, the notebook preview page (the `*-preview.html` behind an embedded notebook's source link) has two fixed-top bars: the site's `#quarto-header` and the preview's `#quarto-embed-header`. Both sit at `top: 0` with the same z-index, and the site header comes later in the DOM, so it paints over the preview bar and hides the back link, the notebook title and the download link. The overlap has been there since notebook previews were introduced. The same happens with a sidebar (its collapsed toggle bar) or an announcement bar.

The overlap can't be fixed in CSS alone because the two bars don't know about each other's height: `quarto-nav.js` offsets the body by the site header height, while the embed template's inline script pads the content by the preview bar height only.

## Fix

The notebook view postprocessor now moves `#quarto-embed-header` into `#quarto-header` as its last child and drops the bar's own `fixed-top` and `headroom` classes. The site navigation script already sizes the body offset from the header height (`ResizeObserver`) and runs Headroom on the whole header, so the embed template's inline script skips its own padding and Headroom setup in that case. This is the same placement approach as the draft alert and the dashboard navigation, which also insert into `#quarto-header`.

Pages without a site header (standalone documents, manuscripts) keep the bar fixed at the top as before.

Two alternatives were rejected: offsetting the two fixed headers separately, which fights Headroom's pin/unpin on each bar, and hiding the site navbar on previews, which loses site navigation.

## Navigation landmark

The preview bar was a plain `<div>`, outside every landmark on pages without a site header, so screen reader users could not reach it through landmark navigation and axe reported it under `region`. It is now a `<nav>` labelled by the notebook title heading through `aria-labelledby`, so the landmark carries the notebook name without a new localized string. It is a `<nav>` rather than a `<header>` because on websites the bar sits inside `#quarto-header`, which is already the page banner.

Both changes touch the same element and template, so they go together here.

The CSS workaround suggested on #14972 is no longer needed once this lands.

Fixes #14972, fixes #14968

title: Fix axe scan hiding the current revealjs slide after navigation
description:
With `axe` enabled in a `revealjs` presentation, moving to another slide while the scan runs leaves the new current slide with `hidden` and `aria-hidden="true"`. Screen readers skip it until the next navigation. With `output: console` or `output: json` nothing navigates after the scan, so the state stays wrong.

## Root cause

Since #14125 (first shipped in v1.9.26), the axe checker removes `hidden` and `aria-hidden` from every slide so axe can check off-screen slides, then puts them back once `axe.run` resolves. The values put back are a snapshot taken before the scan, so a slide change in between gives the new current slide its old hidden state. #15010 already recomputes `inert` from the live Reveal state at that point, but `hidden` and `aria-hidden` were still replayed from the snapshot.

## Fix

`revealRestoreSlides()` in `src/resources/formats/html/axe/axe-check.js` no longer replays the saved values on the current slide and its vertical stack, and uses the same check for `inert`. Other slides get their saved values back, and reveal.js has already hidden the slide that was left.

The new Playwright test navigates as soon as the scan unhides the slides. It fails before the fix, including on v1.10.19, and passes after.

title: Install hyphenation package when babel fails with an undefined language
description:
When rendering to PDF with `lang: de-CH` on a TinyTeX without German hyphenation patterns, Quarto installs `babel-german` but the compilation still fails, and `hyphen-german` is never installed:

```
! Package babel Error: You haven't defined the language 'ngerman' yet.
```

This was first reported in rstudio/tinytex#515, and rstudio/tinytex#516 fixes it in the R package. This PR ports the same changes to Quarto.

## Root cause

Missing hyphenation patterns usually show up as a babel warning, which `findMissingHyphenationFiles()` already handles after a successful compilation. With `lang: de-CH`, babel-german defines `nswissgerman` and then checks `\iflanguage{ngerman}`, which is a fatal error when `hyphen-german` is not installed. The error is not about a missing file, so the `tlmgr search` based detection finds nothing to install.

## Fix

- `findMissingHyphenationPackages()` detects the babel error and the hyphenation package is installed by name with the other missing packages, without a `tlmgr search`.
- Language names are mapped to their package using the `execute AddHyphen` entries of `texlive.tlpdb`. Some names are in a package with another name, e.g. `swissgerman` in `hyphen-german`, `nynorsk` in `hyphen-norwegian`, and all Indic languages in `hyphen-indic`. Only `ngerman` was mapped before. The table was checked against the current `texlive.tlpdb` from CTAN (same 37 names as in rstudio/tinytex#516).
- Names come from the log and are passed to `tlmgr`, so only names matching `^hyphen-[a-z0-9-]+$` are kept. On Windows, `tlmgr.bat` is called through a temporary `.bat` file and `requireQuoting()` does not handle `"`, `%`, `^` or `!`. I did not try to exploit it, this is from reading the code. All hyphenation names in `texlive.tlpdb` pass this filter. It also applies to the existing babel warning detection, which shares the mapping.

The `german-x-*` names from `dehyph-exptl` are not handled, as they are not `hyphen-*` packages. This is the same in rstudio/tinytex#516.

The new smoke test removes `hyphen-german` and `babel-german` before rendering, only on CI, so local runs don't modify the TinyTeX installation.

Fixes #15027

title: Keep dashboard HTML output mistaken for bslib output in its card
description:
## Description

Closes #15023.

The dashboard filter lifts a cell's raw HTML output out of its card when it takes the output for bslib components. It tested for them with `text:match('bslib-')`. In a Lua pattern `-` is a quantifier (zero or more of the preceding character, as few as possible), so the pattern matched any text containing `bsli`, for example:

- the word "subslide";
- `bslib` with no hyphen.

Such output left its card, and a card with nothing else in it was dropped, title included.

The pattern is now `'bslib%-'`. It matches only the literal `bslib-`, the prefix bslib uses in its classes, ids, attributes and custom elements such as `<bslib-tooltip>`.

One real component changes. py-shiny's `ui.accordion()` without an `id` names its elements `bslib_accordion_*` and contains no `bslib-`, so it was lifted only through the loose match. It now stays in its cell's card, with the card's title, like any other output. Two related outputs are still lifted:
- R's `bslib::accordion()`, whose ids are `bslib-accordion-*`;
- a py-shiny accordion given an `id`, which adds the class `bslib-accordion-input`.

Not changed here:
- #14719, where cell options are not applied to real bslib output that is lifted;
- `c:match("^column-")` in `quarto-pre/parsefiguredivs.lua`, which has the same unescaped `-` but is anchored.

### Tests

New `tests/docs/smoke-all/2026/10/11/issue-15023.qmd`, a dashboard with three Python cells:

- the outputs "A subslide of the deck" and "Cards are built by bslib" must stay in the card built from their cell;
- an output with a `bslib-` class must still be lifted out of its cell's card.

The selectors are scoped to `.card.cell`, the card built from a cell. Without the fix all three outputs are lifted, so no cell card is left. The dashboard then wraps the page's loose content, those outputs included, in a card of its own without `.cell`. A selector on `.card` alone, such as `.card .test-subslide`, would match inside that card and pass.

Locally:
- Without the fix, the new test fails on `.card.cell .test-subslide`.
- With the lift disabled (its condition forced to `false`), it fails on `.card.cell .test-lifted`, so the test also catches real bslib output left in its card.
- With the fix, it passes, and so do all 49 smoke-all tests under `docs/smoke-all/dashboard/`.
- A dashboard whose cell outputs `bslib::value_box()` renders byte-identical HTML with and without the fix.

title: Fix notebook preview back link having no href in websites
description:
In website projects the "Back to Article" control of a notebook preview is an `<a>` without `href`. It has no link role and is not in the tab order, so keyboard users cannot go back to the article. Standalone renders are not affected, because they end up with `href=""`.

## Root cause

The `href=""` in standalone renders comes from the `fixEmptyHrefs` HTML postprocessor (`src/core/html.ts`). It is registered in `src/command/render/pandoc.ts` only when the project is not a website. It was added for the tabset cursor in #1227, with a comment saying `quarto-nav.js` does the same in websites. That is not true: `quarto-nav.js` never sets empty hrefs, so website renders never got one.

Using `backHref` alone would not cover the reported case. It is only set when `notebook-preview-options.back` is true, which only manuscripts set by default.

## Fix

The embed template now emits `href` from `backHref` when it is set, and an empty `href` otherwise. The `onclick` handler stays, so the click behavior is unchanged.

Alternatives considered:

- Falling back to `/` was deemed wrong, as it breaks `file://` and sub-path deployments.
- Enabling `fixEmptyHrefs` for websites was deemed too broad. It is a site-wide change and would make the sidebar-collapse anchors in `nav-before-body.ejs` focusable duplicates of the toggle button.

The new Playwright spec fails without the template change and passes with it on chromium and firefox. WebKit was not verified locally, as it never Tabs to links on Windows.

Fixes #15015

title: Keep the closed revealjs slide menu out of the tab order
description:
## Description

Closes #15011.

The bundled menu plugin closes the slide menu by moving it off screen, so while it is closed:

- it stays in the accessibility tree, where screen readers read it as a `navigation` landmark listing every slide;
- once its slide list overflows, Chrome and Firefox make the list a Tab stop, so Tab past the menu button lands on a panel that is not on screen.

`quarto-menu.js` now marks `.slide-menu` `inert` whenever it lacks `active`, the class the plugin toggles to open and close it, and a `MutationObserver` keeps the two in step. It starts on the plugin's `menu-ready` event. With `delay-init: true` the menu is built later, by `initialiseMenu()`, so it then waits for the menu to be added next to `.reveal`.

`visibility: hidden` would not work: `menu.css` sets `visibility: visible` on the active panel, which would keep the slide list exposed. `menu.js` is left alone because it is a single minified line, which #14251 also edits.

### Tests

New decks `menu-focus-order.qmd` (25 slides, so the list scrolls at 1280×720) and `menu-delay-init.qmd`, with tests in `revealjs.spec.ts`:

- Tab from the menu button never lands in the closed menu. The test first checks that the list scrolls.
- The menu still works: M, End and Enter choose a slide, and the button and a click choose another. `inert` is lifted while the menu is open and comes back once it closes; a stuck `inert` would block the click.
- A menu built after load with `delay-init` is inert while closed.

Locally on Chromium, without the fix all 3 new tests fail. With it, all 27 tests in the four `revealjs*.spec.ts` files (including those #15010 added) and the 11 revealjs tests in `axe-accessibility.spec.ts` pass, and in Chrome's accessibility tree the closed menu no longer exposes its landmark or slide entries.

title: Keep revealjs slides that are not on screen out of the tab order
description:
## Description

Fixes #14795.

reveal.js marks slides that are not on screen with `hidden` and `aria-hidden`, but gives the ones within `viewDistance` an inline `display: block` for transitions, which overrides `hidden`. Their links stay in the tab order: on slide 4 of the new test deck, Tab goes to slide 2, slide 3, slide 4, then slide 5.

As discussed in https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/14795#issuecomment-6040554798, the bundled `support` plugin now sets `inert` on every slide except the current one and the stack holding it. It is unconditional, and the condition is the one reveal.js 6.0.2 uses, so it can be dropped when we update:

```js
const allowAllSlides = deck.isOverview() || deck.isScrollView() || deck.isPrintView();
slide.toggleAttribute("inert", !allowAllSlides && slide !== currentSlide && !slide.contains(currentSlide));
```

### When the update runs

- On `ready`, `slidechanged`, `overviewshown` and `overviewhidden`, listened to in the capture phase on `document`. The update then runs before any listener on the deck, including those of plugins registered before `quarto-support`, so a `slidechanged` handler that moves focus into the new slide finds it focusable. This matches reveal.js 6, which updates `inert` before dispatching. A test registers such a listener before any plugin.
- After our own scroll view toggle (`R` and the Tools menu), and after window `resize`, deferred with `setTimeout`. Entering the scroll view does come with a `slidechanged` event, but leaving it dispatches nothing: reveal.js restores the slides' HTML from when the scroll view was entered, and `setState()` goes back to the same indices. reveal's own `resize` event is dispatched only when the scale changes, and before `checkResponsiveScrollView()` switches views in the same `layout()` call. When leaving, it still reports `isScrollView() === true`, so a synchronous handler gets the old state.

### axe

axe-core 4.10 treats `inert` content as hidden from screen readers, so the revealjs scan stopped seeing the other slides (the cross-slide `image-alt` tests failed). `axe-check.js` now lifts `inert` along with `hidden` and `aria-hidden` while scanning, then restores it. It also waits for the deck's `ready` event before scanning, so that slides cannot become inert mid-scan. The report slide, which is added after the scan without a slide change, only becomes inert on the next slide change. It has no focusable content.

### Tests

New deck `tests/docs/playwright/revealjs/tab-order.qmd`, with tests in `revealjs.spec.ts`:

- Tab reaches the current slide's link first: on a deep-linked slide, after navigating, and on a slide in a vertical stack.
- A `slidechanged` listener registered before any plugin can focus the new slide.
- Overview, scroll view (`R`), scroll view on a narrow window, and print view leave every slide reachable, and leaving the overview or scroll view makes the other slides inert again. The scroll view tests move to another slide before leaving, so the restored slides are out of date unless updated.

`axe-accessibility.spec.ts` now also checks that `inert` is restored after the scan.

Locally, on Chromium only:

- Without the fix, 6 of the 8 new tests fail. The listener-order and print view tests guard against regressions in the fix itself.
- With the fix, `revealjs.spec.ts`, `revealjs-themes.spec.ts`, `revealjs-brand.spec.ts`, `revealjs-multiplex.spec.ts`, `axe-accessibility.spec.ts` and the axe unit tests pass. The new tests also passed 10 repeated runs.
- Removing each part of the change fails the test that covers it: the toggle update, the resize handler or its deferral, the capture listener, the overview events, the print view condition, and `contains()`.

title: Make Playwright fixture server port configurable
description:
Playwright tests serve `tests/docs/playwright` with `python -m http.server` on a hardcoded port 8080. Locally, `webServer` uses `reuseExistingServer`, so when another app already listens on 8080 (a very common dev port), Playwright silently uses it instead. Every fixture URL then returns that app's page, and specs fail with element-not-found errors that look like the change under test is broken.

## Fix

The port is now a single constant in `tests/integration/playwright/src/utils.ts`, used by `baseURL`, the `webServer` command and url, and `getUrl()`, so they can't disagree. It reads `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT` and defaults to 8765. Playwright starts the server itself, so nothing relies on 8080, and an uncommon default avoids the collision without any setup. CI needs no change.

`reuseExistingServer` is unchanged. The readiness probe only checks the HTTP status, so it can't tell the fixture server apart from an app answering 200 on every path. When the default port is taken, setting `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT` is the way out.

The Playwright testing rule in `.claude/rules/testing/` is updated with the new port and variable.

## Test plan

- [x] With another app listening on 8080 and `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=8123`, `html-code-tools-toggle.spec.ts` failed on its first locator before this change
- [x] Same setup after the change: `html-code-tools-toggle.spec.ts` passes on the default port and with `QUARTO_PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=8123`

title: Add notice when test-smokes runs without dev knitr/rmarkdown
description:
The `Restore R packages` step in `test-smokes.yml` installs the dev versions of rmarkdown and knitr from r-universe inside `try()`. When this install fails, the version restored by renv stays in place and the tests run against the CRAN release with nothing in the log, so a run can look like it tested dev versions when it did not.

Failing the step was considered but would not catch anything. Both packages are in `tests/renv.lock` and the step already stops when `renv::status()` is not synchronized. In my tests (R 4.6, Windows binaries), a failed `install.packages()` leaves the existing version installed: an unreachable repo only warns and falls back to CRAN from `repos`, and a corrupt archive errors but keeps the previous install. Falling back to CRAN is also the expected tolerance for r-universe flakiness.

So after the install, the step now reads the `Repository` field from each package DESCRIPTION and emits a `::notice::` with the version and source in use when it is not an r-universe URL:

```
::notice::Dev version of knitr not installed; tests use 1.52 from CRAN
```

The source is compared rather than the version, so there is no false positive when dev and CRAN versions are the same right after a release.

I checked the snippet locally against a library with CRAN versions (one notice per package) and one with r-universe versions (no output).

title: Fix keyboard focus reaching off-screen slides in revealjs
description:
In `revealjs` presentations, pressing Tab on the current slide can move focus to links and controls on nearby slides that are not shown. Reveal gives slides within `viewDistance` an inline `display: block`, which defeats the `hidden` attribute, and `aria-hidden` does not affect tab order.

reveal.js fixed this upstream in 6.0.2 (hakimel/reveal.js#1587) by toggling `inert` on every slide that is neither the current slide nor an ancestor of it, except in overview, scroll and print views where all slides are shown. Quarto bundles reveal.js 5.1.0, and moving to 6.x is a separate upgrade, so this adds the same rule to Quarto's `support` plugin. The block is marked for removal once the bundled reveal.js is 6.0.2 or later.

## Fix

`updateInertSlides()` in `support.js` copies reveal's 6.0.2 condition verbatim. It is unconditional, with no format option, and it is skipped in print view. reveal.js 5.1.0 has no hook inside `updateSlidesVisibility()`, so it runs from events:

- `ready` and `slidechanged`. The `slidechanged` listener is registered in the capture phase. `support` registers after format and user plugins, and a plain listener would run after theirs while the new slide is still inert, so a plugin that focuses into the new slide would silently fail.
- `overviewshown` and `overviewhidden`. Inert slides do not receive pointer events, so overview needs it cleared to keep click-to-navigate working.
- A `MutationObserver` on the viewport `class`. Leaving scroll view restores the slides' markup from a snapshot taken on entry, with whatever `inert` values they had then, and reveal.js 5.1.0 dispatches no event when that happens. Scroll from slide 3 to slide 7, leave scroll view, and slide 7 would come back inert and unreachable by keyboard. A `resize` listener does not help for the responsive scroll view, because `resize` fires before the switch.

The axe checker has to follow. It un-hides slides to scan them all, and the bundled axe-core treats `inert` subtrees as hidden, so violations on non-current slides would silently stop being reported. `revealUnhideSlides()` now lifts `inert` as well, and the restore recomputes it from the live reveal state instead of replaying saved values, so a slide change during the scan cannot leave the current slide inert.

Fixes #14795

title: Fix notebook preview files missing from _site when rendering outside the project
description:
When a website with embedded notebooks is rendered from a directory other than the project directory (`quarto render proj/index.qmd` or `quarto render proj` from the parent), `_site/index.html` links to a notebook preview page that is not in `_site`. The same goes for the downloadable notebook source and the figures of the preview. Rendering from inside the project works. This is not a regression: it behaves the same in 1.4, 1.10 and 1.11.

## Root cause

The notebook previewer returns its `supporting` files as project-relative paths, but the HTML post-process contract expects absolute ones (`HtmlPostProcessResult` in `src/format/types.ts`). The render pipeline resolves relative entries against the working directory, so they are dropped unless the working directory happens to be the project directory. Files that are not moved to the output directory are then deleted by the notebook context cleanup. The project-relative handling comes from an earlier path fix that had no test coverage.

## Fix

The previewer now passes absolute supporting paths, and `emplaceNotebookPreviews` only relativizes resource entries that are absolute, since relative ones are already project-relative.

New smoke tests render the site from outside the project for both an `.ipynb` and a `.qmd` embed source, and check that the preview page, notebook source and figures reach `_site`. `testSite` now also removes the project `.quarto` directory so a cached state from one render cannot change a later one.

Fixes #15004

title: Fix embed notebook preview missing from _site on re-render
description:
## Description

When a page embeds a `.qmd` notebook with `embed` and the project is rendered a second time, the embed's preview page and its figure files are missing from `_site`, and the link to the source notebook returns 404.

After the first render, the embedded notebook is revived from its scratch cache in `.quarto/embed/` instead of being rendered again. The preview was then rendered beside the cached copy, inside `.quarto/embed/`, while the output was recorded at its project path. The output relocation skips supporting paths whose source does not exist, so nothing was copied to `_site`. The cache-and-revive path dates from 47269cac6 (2023).

## Fix

A notebook revived from the cache is now copied to `<stem>.embed.ipynb` beside the source, rendered from there, and the copy is removed in a `finally` block. A fresh render writes the same file, so the preview and figure files land where they would on a first render and the existing relocation and cleanup apply unchanged. An existing `<stem>.embed.ipynb` is overwritten, as a fresh render also does.

A notebook revived from the cache is no longer cached again, because caching it nested a second copy at `.quarto/embed/.quarto/embed/`.

The `tests/docs/site/.gitignore` change ignores `**/*.quarto_ipynb` files.

The new test runs from the project directory. A render started from another directory loses the preview independently of this change (#15004), so the test sets `cwd` to the project directory.

## Test Plan

- [x] `smoke/embed/render-embed-website-rerender.test.ts` passes with the fix
- [x] With the fix reverted, the test fails because `_site/source.embed-preview.html` does not exist
- [x] With only the re-caching change reverted, the test fails on the nested `.quarto/embed/.quarto` path
- [x] A manual Python website with `freeze: auto`, rendered three times from the project directory, keeps the preview, the `source.embed_files` figure, and `source.qmd` in `_site` on every render, with no nested cache directory and no leftover `source.embed.ipynb`
- [x] `smoke/embed/render-embed` (3/3), `smoke/site/render-site` (1/1), and `smoke/manuscript/render-manuscript` (5/5) pass

Fixes #10756

title: Fix keyboard navigation of tabsets in HTML documents without Bootstrap
description:
In HTML documents without Bootstrap (`theme: none`), tabsets use Quarto's copy of tabby. Pressing Tab on the selected tab moves focus to the next tab and selects it, so the content of the selected panel is never reachable from the keyboard. Arrow keys do nothing.

## Root cause

`tabby.js` is upstream cferdinandi/tabby v12.0.3, which implements the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (roving tabindex, arrow keys). A 2021 patch adapted it for revealjs, where arrow keys belong to slide navigation: every tab got `tabindex="0"`, a tab became selected on focus, and key handling was limited to Home/End. Only the positive tabindex numbering was scoped to revealjs. The rest applied to every tabby user, including `theme: none` HTML.

## Fix

Outside revealjs, tabby behaves as upstream again: only the selected tab is in the Tab order, arrow keys and Home/End switch tabs, and focus alone does not select a tab. This is the same behavior as Bootstrap tabs. revealjs keeps its current behavior; its focus order is discussed in #14970.

Handled keys now call `preventDefault()` and `stopPropagation()`. Without `preventDefault()`, Firefox and WebKit also scroll the page on Home/End. Without `stopPropagation()`, Home/End on a revealjs tab also reaches reveal's own keyboard handler, so it selects the tab and jumps to the first or last slide. That revealjs bug exists since the 2021 patch and is fixed here too.

revealjs detection keeps the existing `body.reveal-viewport` check rather than `typeof Reveal !== "undefined"`. `Reveal.initialize()` sets this class on the element whose keyboard input reveal drives, so it tells whether reveal owns the arrow keys on the page, while the `Reveal` global only tells that the script was loaded. In Quarto's revealjs output both give the same answer, as tabsets are set up after `Reveal.initialize()`.

Fixes #730

title: Fix logo paths for documents in project subdirectories
description:
When a revealjs or dashboard document is in a project subdirectory, an active brand can cause non-brand logo paths to be treated as project-relative. Extension logos then point outside `_site` and are not copied to `site_libs`; document logos can also break. Brand logos in default projects are affected too.

The shared leading-slash rewrite assumes all logos are project-relative, but only brand logos use that base. Extension, front matter, project metadata, and `_metadata.yml` logos are already document-relative.

Resolve brand paths relative to the input document before merging them with the document logo. For websites, retain a deprecated fallback for project-relative document logos that do not resolve relative to the document, and emit a warning. Regression cases cover encoded paths, query and fragment suffixes, dark-only brands, path collisions, and filenames that cannot be stat'ed. Smoke fixtures also ignore generated files.

Fixes #14946

title: Support lof and lot in Typst documents
description:
Standalone Typst documents ignore `lof: true` and `lot: true`, although the schema advertises both options for Typst. The default template only maps `toc` into `article()`, and Pandoc only honours `lof` and `lot` for LaTeX, ConTeXt and docx, so nothing was ever rendered (#14081).

This adds both lists to the default Typst template, after the table of contents and before the body, as in LaTeX output. They are Typst outlines targeting Quarto's float kinds, `quarto-float-fig` and `quarto-float-tbl`, because Quarto emits floats with those kinds instead of Typst's native `image` and `table`. Titles use the lookup LaTeX already uses: `crossref: lof-title` / `lot-title`, else the localized `crossref-lof-title` / `crossref-lot-title` language strings.

## Design

The lists are rendered inside `article()` rather than by a show rule, so a format that overrides `typst-show.typ` keeps control. orange-book draws its own lists inside `book()` and does not get a second set.

Subfigures are left out of the list of figures in a second commit. Subfloats have the same kind as their parent, so they were listed as separate "Figure 2a" / "Figure 2b" entries. LaTeX lists only the parent, and subpar, which `quarto_super` is adapted from, defaults to `outlined-sub: false`. The rule is scoped to the parent's body, so the parent stays listed and references to a subfigure keep their sub-number. Since `definitions.typ` is shared, this also applies to formats that reuse it for their own lists, such as orange-book.

An extension that ships its own `typst-template.typ` together with Quarto's `typst-show.typ` gets `unexpected argument: lof` only when `lof` is set. This is the same contract `toc-indent` already has.

This covers standalone documents only. The book case needs a fix in the orange-book package first (it looks for `kind: image` and `kind: table`), so #14081 stays open for that.

Part of #14081

title: Add `crossref.numbering: external`; sanction the Lua functions external front ends already call as globals
description:
### Summary

Adds `crossref.numbering: external`, a document-level opt-out that skips Quarto's own
cross-reference numbering, index, and `@ref`-resolution passes, for front ends that
compute their own numbers and just want Quarto's Lua filters to render whatever number
is already on the node. Currently supported for `docx`, `odt`, and `pptx`; `latex`,
`pdf`, `beamer`, and `typst` raise a diagnostic rather than the (previously silent)
malformed output those formats produced when this option reached them.

Also sanctions eight Lua functions — `subrefNumber`, `refPrefix`, `refDelim`,
`refHyperlink`, `refNumberOption`, `crossrefOption`, `renderEquation`, and
`nbspString` — that external front ends already call as undefended bare globals when
reconstructing Quarto's crossref/equation custom nodes outside the normal filter
pipeline. There is existing precedent for this
(`quarto.doc.crossref.decorate_caption_with_crossref`,
`customnodes/floatreftarget.lua:239`); this PR extends the same pattern to the eight
functions actually in use.

Across six commits:

1. **`crossref_present()` / `assign_crossref_numbers()` predicates** — two new
   predicates in a new module, `src/resources/filters/modules/crossref_numbering.lua`,
   answering "should captions/refs still be decorated?" and "should Quarto compute its
   own numbers?" as a function of `enable-crossref` and the new `crossref-numbering`
   param. The existing gates across the crossref filter stage
   (`customnodes/floatreftarget.lua`, `layout/ipynb.lua`, `modules/callouts.lua`) now
   call these instead of checking `enable-crossref` directly.
2. **`enable-crossref: false` scoping + byte-identity verification.** See the scoping
   statement below.
3. **`crossref.numbering: external` reachable from user YAML**: schema entry
   (`src/resources/schema/document-crossref.yml`, enum `[quarto, external]`, default
   `quarto`), the `kCrossrefNumbering` constant (`src/config/constants.ts`), and the
   TypeScript read that puts it on the filter-params blob (`crossrefFilterParams` in
   `src/command/render/crossref.ts`). Without this, the option is only reachable by a
   consumer that builds the params blob itself, not by a `quarto-cli` user setting
   YAML front matter.
4. **Fail fast on `latex`/`pdf`/`beamer`/`typst`.** The predicate in (1) gates the
   entire `quarto_crossref_filters` group, which also runs
   `crossrefMetaInject`'s LaTeX preamble setup (the `codelisting`/theorem environment
   definitions LaTeX output needs) and `resolveRefs`'s Typst `@id`-collision guard
   (Typst has its own native `@id` citation syntax that collides with Quarto's crossref
   `@id` syntax unless resolved first). Neither of those is reachable under
   `enable-crossref: false` today, so skipping them was never previously observable —
   but `crossref.numbering: external` makes the same gate reachable from YAML for any
   format, and a document with a labeled float or theorem then failed deep inside the
   LaTeX or Typst compiler instead of failing cleanly (reproduced: `LaTeX Error:
   Environment codelisting undefined`; Typst `"document does not contain a
   bibliography"`). Fixed by failing fast at the same gate, before Pandoc's writer ever
   sees the malformed intermediate output, naming the unsupported format in the
   diagnostic. New test: `numbering-external-unsupported-format.test.ts`.
5. **Route-N sanctioned exports**: the eight functions named above, exposed as
   `quarto.doc.crossref.*` (all but one) and `quarto.utils.nbspString` (`nbspString` is
   a generic string helper, not crossref-specific):
   - `src/resources/filters/crossref/format.lua`: `subrefNumber`, `refPrefix`,
     `refDelim`, `refHyperlink`, `refNumberOption`
   - `src/resources/filters/crossref/options.lua`: `crossrefOption`
   - `src/resources/filters/crossref/equations.lua`: `renderEquation`
   - `src/resources/filters/common/pandoc.lua`: `nbspString`

   `titlePrefix` (which `refPrefix`/`float_title_prefix` route through) is **not**
   exposed here — it sits outside this list and exposing it is left to whoever needs
   it next. While exposing these, found and fixed a real bug: `refNumberOption`'s
   appendix branch dereferences `crossref.startAppendix`, which is `nil` under external
   mode (it's only ever set inside the group (1) skips) — a direct caller of this
   export would crash. Guarded it to degrade to non-appendix numbering instead;
   `crossref-exports.test.lua` reproduces the crash without the guard and passes with
   it. Also added `lua-types` declarations for all eight exports
   (`lua-types/quarto/{doc,utils}.lua`) and a changelog entry (`news/changelog-1.11.md`)
   — both missing from the original patch, added here.

### Files changed (upstream quarto-cli, all commits)

- `src/resources/filters/modules/crossref_numbering.lua` (new)
- `src/resources/filters/modules/import_all.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/main.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/customnodes/floatreftarget.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/layout/ipynb.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/modules/callouts.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/crossref/format.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/crossref/options.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/crossref/equations.lua`
- `src/resources/filters/common/pandoc.lua`
- `src/resources/lua-types/quarto/doc.lua`
- `src/resources/lua-types/quarto/utils.lua`
- `src/resources/schema/document-crossref.yml`
- `src/config/constants.ts`
- `src/command/render/crossref.ts`
- `src/command/render/pandoc.ts` (unrelated one-line robustness fix picked up in
  passing: guard `captureRenderCommand`'s defaults-YAML rewrite for formats, like
  docx, whose defaults don't reference a template)
- `src/resources/editor/tools/*` (regenerated schema/YAML-intelligence artifacts)
- `news/changelog-1.11.md`
- Tests: `tests/docs/crossrefs/*.qmd` (new fixtures, including
  `numbering-valid.qmd`), `tests/smoke/crossref/*.test.ts` (new + extended, including
  `numbering-external-unsupported-format.test.ts`),
  `tests/smoke/manuscript/render-manuscript.test.ts` (extended),
  `tests/smoke/lua-unit/lua-unit.test.ts` (registers two new Lua unit test files),
  `tests/unit-lua/crossref-numbering.test.lua` (new),
  `tests/unit-lua/crossref-exports.test.lua` (new)

### `enable-crossref: false` scoping statement

`enable-crossref: false` is not user-settable: it is set internally, and only, at
`src/command/render/filters.ts:534`, when `format.render["produce-source-notebook"]`
is true. That flag is in turn only set for manuscript *supporting* notebooks (`.qmd`
files that are not the manuscript's main article — see
`src/project/types/manuscript/manuscript.ts:474-476`), when they are rendered to their
`.out.ipynb` source-notebook form. No other code path in `quarto-cli` sets or reads
this flag as false. So "bit-for-bit on `enable-crossref: false`" means, concretely and
only: the manuscript ipynb-source-notebook outputs (`notebooks/*.out.ipynb` /
`article.out.ipynb`, produced for supporting notebooks in a manuscript project) are
byte-identical, modulo the notebook's own per-cell random UUIDs, before and after this
patch. It is not a claim about any other render path, format, or project type — none
of which can reach `enable-crossref: false` today.

Verified by a two-commit byte-identity procedure (comparand commits `83d48d8e8`
pre-patch, `8061f246a` post-patch): `word/document.xml` and `word/numbering.xml` from a
docx crossref render are byte-identical; the manuscript supporting notebook's
`.out.ipynb` is identical after normalizing out Jupyter's per-cell random UUID (shown
to vary run-to-run on the *same* commit, independent of this patch). No new warnings
appeared in either render's log. This is a dev-only verification procedure, not
committed as a CI script.

### A note on this patch's origin

This PR grew out of work on Quarto 2 (a from-scratch Rust reimplementation currently
in development) — specifically its "Route-N" path, which reconstructs a subset of
Quarto's Pandoc custom AST nodes and re-dispatches them into these filters rather than
reimplementing crossref/equation rendering independently. That context explains why
these particular eight functions and not others, and why `crossref.numbering:
external` exists at all: Route-N needs a way to tell Quarto's filters "render this
number, don't recompute it." Nothing in this PR is Q2-specific — the YAML key, the
schema, and the exports are ordinary `quarto-cli` surface, useful to any front end with
the same need.

### Testing

- `tests/unit-lua/crossref-numbering.test.lua` (10 cases): the 2×2×unknown-value
  cross-product of `crossref_present()` / `assign_crossref_numbers()`.
- `tests/unit-lua/crossref-exports.test.lua` (8 cases, plus the appendix-nil-deref
  regression added in the fix round): one `assertNotNil` per exported name,
  individually named (not a loop over a locally-defined list) so a rename that updates
  both the export and the list can't mask a break in the contract external consumers
  depend on.
- `tests/smoke/crossref/numbering-schema.test.ts`: `crossref.numbering: external`
  passes schema validation; an invalid value fails naming the allowed values.
- `tests/smoke/crossref/numbering-external.test.ts`: full TS → filter-params → Lua
  `param()` path — a docx render with `crossref.numbering: external` keeps the caption
  text but carries no Quarto-assigned "Figure N" prefix, and Lua's numbering pass logs
  the resulting missing `order` field.
- `tests/smoke/crossref/numbering-external-unsupported-format.test.ts`: `--to latex`
  and `--to typst` under `crossref.numbering: external` produce the new diagnostic, not
  a compiler crash.
- `tests/smoke/crossref/callout-order-guard.test.ts`, `tests/smoke/crossref/docx.test.ts`:
  regression coverage for the gate conversions in (1).
- `tests/smoke/manuscript/render-manuscript.test.ts`: extended to assert the manuscript
  supporting-notebook render does not fall through to the generic placeholder
  FloatRefTarget renderer, and that the notebook's figure keeps its identifier/caption
  undecorated (no crossref number) — closes a blind spot in the pre-existing test
  (which only checked output file existence and a log-level filter that doesn't catch
  Lua's INFO-level `warn()` output).
- All of the above pass locally (`cd tests && ./run-fast-tests.sh -k <path>` per file).
  `package/dist/bin/quarto` (no args) typechecks clean.

### Not included in this PR

- Exposing `titlePrefix` as a ninth export.
- Any `_quarto.modules` migration cleanup for `crossref/` (tracked separately as
  `quarto-dev/quarto-cli#14702`; this PR's changes predate that migration reaching
  `crossref/`, and are cheap to make now, expensive after).

title: Typst: resolve CSS generic font families to an installed font
description:
Typst has no generic font families, but `typst_css.lua` passed `serif`, `sans-serif`, `monospace` and the rest straight through. Any `font-family` list or brand typography that used one made Typst warn `unknown font family: sans-serif` on every compile, and Typst then fell back to whatever it liked. `system-ui` and the `ui-*` keywords weren't recognized at all, so they were treated as font names. This is the `system-ui` stack that `gt` tables emit (#11683).

Each generic keyword is now replaced, at its position in the list, by the first installed font from an ordered candidate list. The lists are built from Chromium's per-OS defaults, fontconfig's `60-latin.conf`, Modern Font Stacks and Bootstrap's stacks, with Typst's bundled fonts last so `serif`, `monospace` and `math` always resolve. The keyword itself is never emitted: `font-family: Roboto, sans-serif` becomes `Roboto` if it's installed, and otherwise the first installed sans-serif candidate. The candidate lists live in `typst_css.lua`, with their sources cited. No fonts are bundled.

When nothing in a generic's list is installed (realistically `sans-serif` on a bare Linux box), the keyword is dropped. If that leaves the list empty, we use Typst's default text font, because Typst rejects an empty `font: ()`. `generic(...)` is dropped, since Typst has no equivalent.

The winning font differs per machine, so the smoke-all fixtures assert only that a concrete family is emitted and that no generic keyword reaches the `.typ`. `font-filtering-generics` previously asserted that the keyword was preserved, which is the behavior this changes.

This is a backport of quarto-dev/q2#788.

This replaces #11918, which mapped each generic to one fixed font and bundled Noto Sans, and #14592, which dropped generics from the list but still warned when a list contained only generics.

Fixes #11683.

title: fix(pandoc): Merge project metadata with document front matter
description:
## Description

Continues #13353, whose author handed the branch over (his commits are kept with authorship). A key defined both in a document's front matter and in `_quarto.yml` or `metadata-files` reaches Pandoc templates and Lua filters with only the document's value. Setting `params.nested.A` in a document drops `params.nested.B` coming from the project, and a project array such as `keywords` loses its project entries. This was first reported in discussion quarto-dev/quarto-cli#11138 and is #11139. The same loss hits an author list from a directory `_metadata.yml` combined with an author in a post's front matter, reported in #9864.

`options.format.metadata` already holds the correct merge. The loss happens in `runPandoc`, which re-applies each top-level key of the executed front matter with a plain assignment so that knitr inline R in YAML is resolved in the output (added in 2021 for that purpose). The assignment replaces whatever the project contributed to the key.

For a key that execution left unchanged, the front matter as written is now merged on top of the resolved value. Other sources keep the leaves and list entries the document does not set, and the document still wins the ones it does. The input's metadata as written is passed to `runPandoc` as `unexecutedMetadata` to tell unchanged keys from keys holding inline expressions. A key with an inline expression takes the executed value as a whole, so the project's children of such a key are still lost. This is a known limit of working per top-level key.

Lists now combine the same way for every key. Before, `keywords`, `tags` and other keys passed through here replaced the project's list with the document's, while Quarto's own keys such as `css` already combined, as the documentation says. As a side effect, a document can no longer clear an inherited list with an empty value (`keywords: ""` or `[]`), which only worked because of the re-apply step. There is no replacement for it for now, the same as for `css`.

Merging the front matter on top, rather than substituting the leaves execution changed, keeps the documented precedence: `options.format.metadata` merges the document first and `metadata-files` after it, so a leaf substitution would let a metadata file win over the front matter. Substituting leaves also duplicated an array entry when an inline expression evaluated to a value the project already listed. The merge wraps the values in an object because `mergeConfigs` on two bare arrays merges them by index.

Putting the document's value back means a top-level `controls: auto` or `previewLinks: auto` would replace the `false` that the revealjs format computes for them, and reveal.js would receive a bare `auto` identifier, which was already the case before this change. Both keys are skipped for revealjs when the value is not a boolean, like `theme`, and a boolean set in the front matter still wins over `metadata-files`.

The first commit adds characterization tests, passing on `main`, for what the re-apply step already protects: format-level keys, knitr inline R in YAML (also with frozen results), book chapter titles and website categories. The remaining tests cover the merge itself: project and document keys, `metadata-files`, the `--metadata-file` option, an author list from a directory `_metadata.yml` combined with a document author, and revealjs `controls` and `previewLinks`.

Fixes #11139, fixes #9864, supersedes #13353

title: Ignore detect paths that can't be stat'ed in project detection
description:
## Description

Fixes #14983.

Project detection currently treats an inaccessible detect path as if it exists. This happens because `safeExistsSync`, which wraps `@std/fs`’s `existsSync`, returns `true` for `PermissionDenied`.

As a result, a parent directory containing `content/` and an inaccessible `config/` can incorrectly match Hugo’s `config/_default/config.toml` detect path, even when that file does not exist. `quarto render` may then:

- write `hugo-md` output despite `--output doc.html`; or
- fail while walking the directory.

This change counts a detect path only when `Deno.statSync` succeeds. It affects detection only; the input walk still fails on unreadable directories, as intended by #14966.

**Scope.** Quarto resolves documents using absolute paths, so every directory in the upward walk must be searchable. A `_quarto.yml` or single-segment detect path is checked in a searchable directory, so a permission error cannot cause a false match there. Among the bundled extensions, only Hugo’s multi-segment detect path (`config/_default/config.toml`) is affected.

**Trade-off.** If a Hugo site’s `config/` directory cannot be searched, Quarto will no longer detect it as a Hugo site and will render the input as a single file. If only the config file itself is unreadable, the site is still detected (tested on macOS and Linux).

**Tests.** Added unit and smoke tests that fail without this change and pass with it, on macOS and in CI. The following also pass:

- `tests/unit/project`
- `smoke/project/project-unreadable-dir`
- the project `check` tests from #14966
- `deno fmt --check`
- `deno lint`

Added one sentence describing this rule to `llm-docs/project-context-architecture.md`.

title: Fix scroll position reset by Safari scrollbar workaround
description:
Pages with a light and a dark theme can open at the top in Safari instead of at the URL fragment, and toggling the color scheme mid-page sends the reader back to the top (#14973).

## Root Cause

The Safari scrollbar workaround from #1455 (scrollTo(0, 1), then scrollTo(0, 0) after 40 ms) lives inside `toggleColorMode()`. The color scheme script also calls that function at the start of `<body>` on every page load, so the workaround ran on load too. Its 40 ms timer can fire after Safari has already scrolled to the fragment target, and the absolute `scrollTo(0, 0)` then undoes that scroll. The same absolute `scrollTo(0, 0)` also moved readers to the top when they toggled the scheme mid-page.

Saving `scrollY` before the first `scrollTo`, as suggested in the issue, would not fix the load case: at the start of `<body>` `scrollY` is still 0.

## Fix

The workaround moves into `refreshSafariScrollbar()`, called only from `window.quartoToggleColorScheme` and the `prefers-color-scheme` listener. It is not needed on load, because the stylesheets are already set before first paint there, so there is no stale scrollbar to refresh. On a toggle it nudges one pixel from the current `scrollY` and returns to it, so the reader stays where they were.

Playwright specs cover both cases. The load test is WebKit-only: its Safari user agent is what triggers the workaround, and it fails there without the change. Both specs pass on all three browsers with it.

Real macOS Safari is unverified. Whether the 1px nudge still recolors the scrollbar (#1455) needs a check on a Mac.

Fixes #14973

title: Don't save renv and Typst caches after an interrupted restore
description:
When a `test-smokes.yml` job is cancelled while `actions/cache/restore` is still extracting the renv cache, the "Save Renv package cache" step uploads the half-extracted directory under the exact primary key. Every later run on that branch gets an exact cache hit, so the save step never runs again and the partial cache stays until the entry is deleted by hand.

This happened on v1.10. A cancelled Windows job (run 37319490760) saved a 196 MB cache over the 347 MB entry it was extracting, and later runs failed the knitr SQL docs with `'DBI' is not a valid installed package`. main stayed green on the same `renv.lock` because branch-scoped cache entries take precedence over main's. The bad entry has been deleted, but nothing prevents this from happening again, on main as well.

## Root cause

Both the renv and Typst save steps use `always() && cache-hit != 'true'`. `always()` includes cancelled jobs, and an interrupted restore never sets `cache-hit`. The `renv::status()` check in "Restore R packages" doesn't catch the result: on the poisoned cache, renv linked DBI from the truncated copy and status still reported the library as synchronized.

The condition was taken from `r-lib/actions/setup-renv` when moving off the deprecated `save-always`, and it is still the same there.

## Fix

The renv save now requires the "Restore R packages" step to have succeeded. That step is skipped when the cache restore was interrupted, cancelled when `renv::restore()` is interrupted, and failed when the library ends up out of sync. The Typst save gets the same rule on its own restore step. `!cancelled()` replaces `always()` instead of being dropped, so caches are still saved when tests fail.

`julia-actions/cache` follows the same rule: it doesn't save unless its restore completed.

This needs a backport to v1.10, where the poisoning happened.

## Test plan

- [x] Forced a renv cache miss on a throwaway branch (renamed key segment), dispatched `test-smokes.yml` and cancelled it while Windows was in "Restore R packages" (run 37341236232). Both save steps were skipped on Windows (cancelled during the R restore) and on Ubuntu (cancelled before it), and no cache entry was created for the branch. With the previous condition, this cache miss would have saved.

title: Make scrollable code blocks and cell output keyboard-focusable in HTML output
description:
Closes #14378. Part of #8706.

## What this does

A code block or cell output that overflows is scrollable, but keyboard users cannot reach or scroll it in Safari. Chrome and Firefox already make such regions focusable natively, so this is a Safari gap for users and a missing accessible name everywhere. axe reports `scrollable-region-focusable` (serious, WCAG 2.1.1/2.1.3) in all three, because it reads markup rather than browser behavior. Compatibility under Design notes has the detail.

This adds a runtime module to `quarto.js`, for bootstrap HTML formats only. While a region overflows it gets `tabindex="0"`, `role="group"`, a localized `aria-label`, and a `data-quarto-scrollable` marker so removal only touches attributes we added. The attributes come off when the region fits again. The sync runs on `DOMContentLoaded` and from the existing body `ResizeObserver`, so it adds no new observers. That observer's throttle now also makes a trailing call, so the last resize of a burst is synced. The margin layout and the reader-mode check share that callback, so they get the fix too. The TOC and sidebar scroll handlers keep the old leading-edge-only throttle.

The candidates are the three scroll containers in rendered HTML:

| Candidate | Overflow source |
|---|---|
| `div.sourceCode` | Pandoc's `div.sourceCode { overflow: auto }` for highlighted code |
| `pre` | Bootstrap reboot's `pre { overflow: auto }` |
| `.cell-output-display:not(.no-overflow-x)` | [`_quarto-rules.scss`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/1f4ff1871010c559d33719d4a9251c6afb6e131b/src/resources/formats/html/_quarto-rules.scss#L384-L387) |

## Which regions get marked

A region qualifies when its computed overflow is `auto` or `scroll`, which is axe's own condition, and it overflows by more than 1px. Three kinds of region are skipped:

- **Author markup**, meaning an existing `tabindex` or `aria-label`.
- **No usable size**: a closed `<details>`, an inactive tab pane, or a `visually-hidden` code alternative. The last is clipped to 1px, which makes its content height read as overflow. Marking it would add an invisible tab stop, and quarto-web's get-started pages carry about nine each.
- **Real focusable content**, such as a link in a wide table, which the browser already scrolls into view.

Pandoc's line anchors are the exception to that third rule. Without line numbers they carry `tabindex="-1"`, so they are out of the tab order anyway. With line numbers they are real focusable links, kept that way on purpose by #14655. But each one sits at the start of its line, so focusing it leaves `scrollLeft` at 0 and the clipped content unreachable. A numbered block therefore satisfies axe while staying unscrollable, so it gets its own region tab stop alongside its per-line links.

## When it re-syncs

One rule, not one per widget: the module re-syncs when the page's layout changes size. Collapsed callouts, folded `<details>`, and tab panes of differing heights all make the page taller, so a single `ResizeObserver` covers them with no mechanism-specific code.

The boundary is a reveal that changes no size, and two tab panes of equal height are the clean example. That case keeps today's behavior rather than regressing anything. A `shown.bs.tab` hook would fix tabsets while still missing equal-height accordions and overlay panels, trading one documented boundary for a special case plus a boundary.

## Design notes

**Runtime JS, not a static `tabindex`.** A Lua filter would put a tab stop on every code block, whether or not it scrolls. It would also change the markup of every code block, which breaks scrapers and element-level snapshot tests. Here the element markup stays unchanged. Each page does gain one short script that carries the labels (see Labels), so a snapshot of the whole page still sees a diff.

**Compatibility.** Chrome (since 132, January 2025) and Firefox already make these regions focusable natively ([Chrome blog](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/keyboard-focusable-scrollers)). These tab stops have therefore been live on every Quarto site for over a year, with no reports. That bounds the risk: this polyfills shipped browser behavior rather than inventing a new interaction. What it adds on top is Safari coverage, an accessible name, and axe conformance. Every failure mode leaves an element exactly as it is today.

**Labels.** Two new language keys, `scrollable-code-label` and `scrollable-output-label`. `quarto.js` is static, so the after-body script passes the resolved strings through a window global. The module falls back to the English defaults.

**`role="group"`, not `region`.** Pages carry many code blocks, and `region` landmarks would flood the screen-reader rotor.

## Tests

- 15 unit tests (`tests/unit/scrollable-regions.test.ts`): overflow geometry, usable size, the focusable-content rule, label merging.
- 16 Playwright tests (`tests/integration/playwright/tests/html-scrollable-regions.spec.ts`) on chromium, firefox, and webkit: marking and removal across viewports, the last resize of a burst, the three skips, one tab stop per block, real-Tab reach with a visible focus ring, and arrow-key scrolling. A second fixture (`scrollable-regions-labels.qmd`) checks that a `lang: fr` label and a `language:` override holding `</script>` both reach `aria-label` intact. Arrow keys are asserted on chromium and firefox only, because Playwright's WebKit routes them to the page even when a scroller has focus.
- `axe-accessibility` still passes (116 tests), with its code-line-number fixtures re-rendered.
- On quarto-web pages rendered with this build, the violations on `about.html` (`#cb1`) and `docs/troubleshooting/index.html` (bare `pre`) are gone, and axe reports none for the rule at 390x844.
- A full sync costs 0.6ms median on a 200-block page (400 candidates), against the existing 50ms throttle.

title: Fix Typst brand font dropped after rendering a sibling document
description:
## Description

When two documents sharing a `.quarto` directory use different brand Google fonts with Typst, the second render can drop its brand font from the `font:` list. This is a regression from #14580 (first shipped in 1.10.10), which filters unavailable fonts out of Typst font-family lists using the output of `typst fonts`.

That output is cached in memory and in `.quarto/typst/available-fonts.json`, keyed on a hash of the font path strings. Brand Google fonts always download into the same `.quarto/typst/fonts` directory, so the key never changes and a later render reuses the font list of an earlier one. The newly downloaded font is then treated as unavailable. A project whose brand font changes between renders is affected the same way, and this is how `font-list.qmd` failed in CI when `title-inherit-base-family.qmd` ran before it in the same bucket.

The cache key is now a hash of the contents of every directory Typst searches (relative path, size and mtime of each file), so adding a font invalidates both caches. The directories come from `fontPathsArgs`, which also covers user `font-paths`, brand `source: file` directories and `TYPST_FONT_PATHS`. Directory mtimes alone were not enough: on NTFS, adding a file deep in `fonts.gstatic.com/s/<family>/<version>/` changes neither the top directory nor `s/`.

The new file system access must never make a render fail. A missing font directory gets a stable marker in the key (Typst ignores missing paths), and an entry that cannot be stat'd is recorded as such without dropping the rest. If the scan fails for any other reason, both caches are bypassed and `typst fonts` is queried directly rather than reusing a possibly stale list.

The unit tests that add a fixture font assert it is absent first, so a host that already has that font installed fails on that precondition instead of passing falsely. The new smoke test renders two documents in one directory. Against a built Quarto (`QUARTO_TEST_BIN`) each render is its own process, which exercises the disk cache as in the CI failure.

Fixes #14993

title: Fix metadata footnotes shifting heading levels in PDF and Typst
description:
With a footnote in `title`, `subtitle` or `author`, PDF output with `number-sections: true` and Typst output shift heading levels even though the document has level-1 headings. The first `#` heading becomes the document title and `##` headings are numbered as top-level sections.

Quarto decides whether to add `shift-heading-level-by: -1` with `hasLevelOneHeadings()`, which runs the document through Pandoc with `leveloneanalysis.lua` and expects the output to be exactly `true`. The filter replaced the body with `true` or `false` but kept the metadata, and Pandoc's markdown writer still writes the notes it collected from metadata. The output became `true` followed by `[^1]: ...` and the check failed. Any footnote in the front matter triggers it, not only in title and author.

The filter now also clears the metadata, so only `true` or `false` is written. This only affects the Pandoc run used for the check, the document metadata in the actual render is untouched. Headings are counted before the metadata is cleared, so the result for documents with only level-2 headings and for `#` comments in code blocks (#11835) is unchanged.

Typst is affected even without `number-sections`, as its caller doesn't check it (`src/format/typst/format-typst.ts:98`).

Fixes #14982

title: Make the collapsible callout header a keyboard-accessible button
description:
## Description Fixes #4934. The header of a collapsible callout was a `
` with `aria-expanded`, no role, and no tab stop. Its `aria-label="Toggle callout"` also hid the title from screen readers. The header now wraps the icon, title, and chevron in a native `
``` - Keyboard users can reach the toggle with Tab and operate it with Enter or Space. - The name of the button is the callout type and the title, for example "Note Title". - The button target stays the `.callout-N-contents` class. Margin content that moves out of the callout keeps this class, so it still collapses with the callout. - The hidden type label now ends with a space. Without it, the button name was "NoteTitle". - Bootstrap updates `collapsed` on the trigger only. Thus the corner-radius rule now uses `:has(> .callout-toggle-btn.collapsed)` instead of a class on the header. **No visual change.** I rendered 48 callouts with `main` and with this branch: all types, the default, simple, and minimal appearances, collapsed and expanded, static callouts, and margin content. All screenshots are pixel-identical in Chromium and WebKit, before and after a toggle. The only new visual is the focus ring on keyboard focus. **axe:** the `aria-allowed-attr` finding (35 instances on the test page) is gone. A link in a collapsible title is now inside the button, so axe reports `nested-interactive`. Authors must not put links in a collapsible title. **Custom CSS:** selectors for collapsible callouts change. `.callout-header[aria-expanded]` and `.callout-header.collapsed` become `.callout-toggle-btn[aria-expanded]` and `.callout-toggle-btn.collapsed`. The icon and title containers are now ``, so `div.callout-title-container` no longer matches collapsible callouts. A GitHub code search found no hand-written CSS that uses the old header selectors. The one script it found adds `role="button"` to the header, which is a workaround for this issue. The changelog entry states the change. ## Checklist I have (if applicable): - [x] referenced the GitHub issue this PR closes - [x] updated the appropriate changelog in the PR - [x] ensured the present test suite passes - [x] added new tests - [ ] created a separate documentation PR in [Quarto's website repo](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-web/) and linked it to this PR Tests: a smoke-all test for the markup (`callouts/a11y/issue-4934.qmd`) and a Playwright keyboard test (`html-callouts.spec.ts`).
